definition_zh: 指控；控告；（在司法程序中）起诉；把过错归到某人头上
definition_en: to say that a person or group has done something wrong or illegal, especially as a formal charge in court
core_image: 法庭上，检察官抬起手，隔着房间指向被告席，把一页罪的清单递到法官面前
scene: 法庭里，检察官把一摞污染检测记录放在桌上，抬手指向被告席上的厂方代表。The prosecutor accused the factory of dumping chemical waste into the river.
sceneCN: 这里 accuse 指在司法程序中对人或机构提出正式指控（第 1 个义项：在法庭上控告某人犯罪）；句意为检察官指控这家工厂向河里倾倒化学废料。图中可辨识物件：起诉卷宗、检测记录、被告席、法官席。

pos.zh: 指控；控告；指责（常与 of 连用）
（作名词时）被指控者；刑事被告

derivatives.zh: 指责口吻的；控告性质的

senses.title: Bring a charge in court
senses.titleCN: 在法庭上提出刑事指控
senses.definition: to charge someone formally before a court with a crime
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上正式指控某人犯有某项罪行
senses.example: The prosecutor accused the factory of dumping chemical waste into the river.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官指控这家工厂向河里倾倒化学废料。
senses.why: The Latin verb began as a legal move: ad- 'to' plus causa 'lawsuit' meant to bring a case against someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词最初就是法庭动作：ad-「朝向」加 causa「案由」，意为把案子提到某人身上。

senses.title: Blame for an ordinary fault
senses.titleCN: 日常责备，把过错归到某人
senses.definition: to say that someone is to blame for something that went wrong
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人应对某件出错的事负责并加以责备
senses.example: She accused her brother of breaking the window and never apologising.
senses.exampleCN: 她指责弟弟打破窗户却从不道歉。
senses.why: The courtroom sense moved into the home and the office, where naming a culprit needs no judge.
senses.whyCN: 法庭义进入家庭与办公室，在这些场合指认过错方并不需要法官。

senses.title: Aim the charge at a system
senses.titleCN: 把责任指向制度、政策等抽象对象
senses.definition: to name a policy, institution or period as the cause of a problem
senses.definitionCN: 把某项政策、机构或时代指认为问题的成因
senses.example: Critics accuse the zoning rules of deepening the housing crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指责分区规则加深了住房危机。
senses.why: Once a charge can be laid on a person, it can also be laid on a rule that behaves like a person.
senses.whyCN: 罪名既然可以落在一个人身上，也就可以落在一条像人一样起作用的规则上。

senses.title: Name a specific wrongdoing
senses.definition: to state the exact act a person is said to have committed, usually with of
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人被说成做过的具体行为，通常与表示「关于」的介词搭配
senses.example: The report accused two managers of falsifying safety records.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指控两名经理伪造安全记录。
senses.why: The preposition of fixes the charge to one deed, which is why the pattern accuse someone of something is so stable.
senses.whyCN: 这个介词把指控钉在一件具体的事上，因此「指控某人做了某事」这一结构非常固定。

senses.title: Assert without proof
senses.titleCN: 仅凭怀疑断言，尚未举证
senses.definition: to assert guilt even though no proof has yet been produced
senses.definitionCN: 在尚无证据的情况下断言某人有罪
senses.example: He accused her in front of the whole team, though nothing was ever proved.
senses.exampleCN: 他当着整个团队的面指责她，尽管从未得到证实。
senses.why: A charge can be spoken before evidence arrives, so the verb also carries the weaker sense of merely asserting.
senses.whyCN: 指控可以先于证据说出口，因此这个词也带上了「只是断言」的弱化含义。

senses.title: Point without words
senses.titleCN: 神情或沉默本身在责怪人
senses.definition: to express blame through a look, a tone or silence rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 以眼神、语气或沉默而非言语表达责备
senses.example: Her raised eyebrow accused him more sharply than any sentence could.
senses.exampleCN: 她挑起眉毛，比任何一句话都更尖锐地责怪了他。
senses.why: Blame is a gesture before it is a sentence, so a face can do the accusing.
senses.whyCN: 责备在成为句子之前首先是一个动作，因此一张脸也能完成指控。

senses.title: Turn the charge inward
senses.definition: to blame oneself, often in a private or literary way
senses.definitionCN: 把指责转向自己，多用于内心或文学性的表达
senses.example: He accused himself of cowardice long after the others had forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 别人早已忘记，他却长久地责备自己怯懦。
senses.why: The same verb serves when the accuser and the accused are one person.
senses.whyCN: 当指控者与被指控者是同一个人时，用的仍是同一个动词。

senses.title: The person under charge
senses.definition: the accused: the person against whom a criminal charge is brought
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时，指被提起刑事指控的人
senses.example: The accused sat quietly while the clerk read the charge aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员大声宣读指控时，被告安静地坐着。
senses.why: A past participle turned into a noun, a familiar English habit: the person charged becomes the accused.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词转成名词是英语常见的做法：被指控的人于是成了「被告」。

intro.en: Accuse reaches English through Old French from Latin accusare 'to call to account, bring a charge', built on ad- 'to' and causa 'lawsuit, reason'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: accuse 经古法语来自拉丁 accusare「传唤问罪、提出控告」，由 ad-「朝向」与 causa「案由、理由」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Causa named a legal case or the reason behind it; the same noun also gives English cause and forms the second half of accuse.
items.cn: causa 指一桩案子或案子背后的理由；同一个名词也构成英语 cause，并是 accuse 的后半部分。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus causa produced accusare 'to bring a charge against, call to account'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 causa 构成 accusare「对某人提出控告、传唤问罪」。

items.en: Old French shortened the verb to acuser and passed it into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把动词简作 acuser，并在十三世纪把它带入英语。

items.en: The earliest English records are legal: the verb named the act of charging someone before a court.
items.cn: 英语最早的书证属于法律语境：这个动词指在法庭上对某人提出指控。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb had spread to ordinary quarrels, and the noun use the accused settled into court reporting.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已扩展到日常争吵，指「被告」的名词用法也固定进法庭报道。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of causa is unsettled, so any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction; the exact first citation is also uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：causa 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的更古老词根都属于重构形式；确切的最早书证同样不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stock that are easily mistaken for one another; group two holds verbs of blaming that differ in force and in legal weight.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干、极易互相混淆的词；第二组是责备类动词，力度与法律分量不同。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out of' plus causa: to take someone out of a charge, hence to forgive or to offer a reason.
entries.definitionCN: ex-「出」加 causa：把人从指控里拿出来，因此指原谅或给出理由。

entries.tag: same root, a judge steps aside
entries.definition: Re- 'back' plus causa: a judge withdraws from a case because of a conflict of interest.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 causa：法官因利益冲突而从案件中退出。

entries.definition: The Latin noun itself, meaning reason or case, and the source of the second half of accuse.
entries.definitionCN: 这就是那个拉丁名词本身，意为理由或案子，也是 accuse 后半部分的来源。

entries.definition: A grammatical case name derived from the same verb; it labels the object of a verb, not a person on trial.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词派生的语法术语，指宾格，标的是动词的宾语，而不是受审的人。

entries.definition: The standard legal verb for bringing an accusation, often used in the passive in police reports.
entries.definitionCN: 提出控告的标准法律动词，警方通报中常用被动式。

entries.definition: From Latin indicere 'to declare': to bring a formal criminal charge, usually after a grand jury finding.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 indicere「宣告」：提出正式刑事指控，通常在大陪审团认定之后。

entries.definition: The plain verb for holding someone responsible; it carries no legal procedure and no formal charge.
entries.definitionCN: 归责于人的日常动词，不含法律程序，也不构成正式指控。

entries.definition: To assert that something is true or that someone did wrong, with the emphasis on the lack of proof.
entries.definitionCN: 断言某事为真或某人做错，重点在于尚无证据。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus causa 'case': to put a case onto someone.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 causa「案子」：把案子搁到某人身上。

normal.en: The family runs accuse, accusation, accuser, accusing, accusatory, the accused.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 accuse、accusation、accuser、accusing、accusatory，以及指「被告」的名词用法。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal core: accuse someone of something, stand accused of.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律内核：指控某人做了某事、被指涉嫌。

normal.en: Excuse and recuse share the same causa but move the charge away from the person.
normal.cn: excuse 与 recuse 用的是同一个 causa，但都把指控从人身上移开。

normal.en: News style keeps the passive: the company was accused of hiding the leak.
normal.cn: 新闻语体偏爱被动式：该公司被指隐瞒泄漏。

abstract.en: Picture a finger that never touches the person it points at.
abstract.cn: 想象一根始终不碰到对方的手指，却一直指着对方。

abstract.en: Picture a word spoken before the proof arrives, like a letter sent before the facts.
abstract.cn: 想象一句在证据到来之前就说出口的话，像事实未到就寄出的信。

abstract.en: Picture the same hand turning to point at its own chest.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手转过来，指向自己的胸口。

examples.en: The inquiry accused the agency of hiding the report.
examples.cn: 调查指控该机构藏起了那份报告。

examples.en: The coach accused the players of giving up in the second half.
examples.cn: 教练指责球员在下半场放弃了比赛。

examples.en: In the novel the narrator accuses himself of every fault he sees in others.
examples.cn: 小说里，叙述者把自己在别人身上看到的每个毛病都归到自己头上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a（一）+ cause（缘由）」——抓住一个缘由就指着人说：指控、指责

root: 拉丁 accusare「提出控告」= ad-（朝向）+ causa「案由、理由」；causa 更深来源不确定。英语 accuse 经古法语 acuser 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand: it points at an offender in court, then at a relative, a policy, a single deed, a suspicion, a silence, and finally at the speaker himself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一只手：先在法庭指向罪犯，再指向亲人、政策、一件具体的事、一份怀疑、一段沉默，最后指向说话者自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised in a courtroom, pointing across the room at the one being charged.
core.cn: 核心意象：法庭上一只抬起的手，隔着房间指向被控的一方。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: the charge is spoken by an official voice and written down by a clerk.
branches.cn: 法庭：指控由官方之口说出，并由书记员记下。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY CHARGE: at home or in public debate the finger points at a relative, then at a rule.
branches.cn: 日常指控：在家里或公共争论中，手指先指向亲人，再指向一条规则。

branches.en: THE DEED NAMED: the preposition of pins the blame to one act rather than a vague dislike.
branches.cn: 点明的事：表示「关于」的介词把责备钉在一件具体行为上，而非笼统的反感。

branches.en: WITHOUT PROOF: a charge may be asserted early or delivered by a look alone.
branches.cn: 没有证据：指控可以早早说出口，也可以只由一个眼神送达。

branches.en: WHO CHARGES WHOM: the accuser may be the accused, and the accused is a person with a seat in court.
branches.cn: 谁指控谁：指控者可以就是被指控者，而被告是法庭上有一个座位的人。

intro.en: Accuse is a Latin verb whose prefix and root both build other English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: accuse 是一个拉丁动词，前缀与词根各自还构成别的英语词，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin causa gives cause, excuse and recuse as well as the second half of accuse; ad- adds direction toward a target.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 causa 除构成 accuse 的后半部分，还衍生 cause、excuse 与 recuse；ad- 增添「朝向目标」的方向。

items.structure: ad- (Latin prefix, assimilated to ac- before c)
items.example: The prefix directs the charge at a target.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把指控指向一个对象。

items.example: The root supplies both the case and the reason for it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时提供案子与案子的理由。

items.example: The prosecutor accused the factory.
items.exampleCN: 检察官指控了这家工厂。

items.meaning: the act or result of charging
items.example: The accusation was never proved.
items.exampleCN: 这项指控从未得到证实。

items.example: The accuser refused to be named.
items.exampleCN: 指控者拒绝透露姓名。

items.structure: accuse + -ed (past participle used as a noun)
items.example: The accused entered the courtroom.
items.exampleCN: 被告走进了法庭。

items.example: She gave him an accusing glance.
items.exampleCN: 她责备地看了他一眼。

items.example: His letter was accusatory in tone.
items.exampleCN: 他那封信语气带着指控意味。

definition_zh: 指控；指称；（未经证实的）说法；诉状中的主张
definition_en: a statement that someone has done something wrong, made without proof
core_image: 一份还没盖章的控诉纸被推到桌子中央，等着有人去核实
scene: 记者会上，发言人把一份尚未核实的举报材料举起来，说明其中列出的问题还待调查。The newspaper printed the allegation without naming its source.
sceneCN: 这里 allegation 指尚未得到证实的指称（第 1 个义项：未经证实的违法或不当行为指控）；句意为报纸刊登了这项指控，却没有交代消息来源。图中可辨识物件：举报材料、录音笔、麦克风、未署名的页脚。

pos.zh: 指控；指称；（未经证实的）说法
（诉状、调查文书中的）主张；控诉要点

senses.title: Unproved charge of wrongdoing
senses.titleCN: 未经证实的违法或不当行为指控
senses.definition: a claim that someone has done something illegal or wrong, made before any proof is offered
senses.definitionCN: 在证据出现之前提出的、指某人违法或做错事的说法
senses.example: The newspaper printed the allegation without naming its source.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸刊登了这项指控，却没有交代消息来源。
senses.why: Allegation is the noun of allege, whose Latin source meant 'to bring forward, adduce'; what is brought forward is not yet proved.
senses.whyCN: allegation 是 allege 的名词，其拉丁来源意为「提出、援引」；被提出来的东西尚未得到证明。

senses.title: A claim stated in pleadings
senses.titleCN: 诉状或正式文书中的主张
senses.definition: a formal statement of facts asserted in a legal pleading
senses.definitionCN: 在诉讼文书中正式陈述、待举证的事实主张
senses.example: The allegation in the complaint must be answered point by point.
senses.exampleCN: 诉状中的每项主张都必须逐条答辩。
senses.why: In procedure a pleading sets out allegations, and the other side must admit or deny each of them.
senses.whyCN: 在诉讼程序中，诉状列出一项项主张，对方必须逐条承认或否认。

senses.title: Any assertion, not only of guilt
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true, whether or not it concerns wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 作为真实提出的说法，未必涉及罪责
senses.example: The allegation that the earth moves was once treated as dangerous.
senses.exampleCN: 「大地会动」这一说法一度被视为危险。
senses.why: The word keeps the bare sense of something asserted, which is why it can appear outside courts and police reports.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「被提出的说法」这一基本义，因此可以出现在法庭与警方通报之外。

senses.title: A string of charges
senses.titleCN: 复数形式指一连串指控
senses.definition: a series of charges made together, often in a report or investigation
senses.definitionCN: 成组提出的多项指控，多见于报道或调查
senses.example: The audit listed allegations of overcharging, nepotism and falsified invoices.
senses.exampleCN: 审计列出了一连串指控：超额收费、任人唯亲与伪造发票。
senses.why: Reporters count allegations in the plural when a single case produces several separate claims.
senses.whyCN: 当一桩案子引出多项彼此独立的说法时，报道会用复数来计数。

senses.title: The act of bringing a charge
senses.titleCN: 提出指控这一行为本身
senses.definition: the act of making a charge rather than the charge itself
senses.definitionCN: 指提出指控的动作，而非指控的内容
senses.example: Allegation of misconduct is a formal step that starts the disciplinary process.
senses.exampleCN: 提出不当行为指控是一个正式步骤，会启动纪律程序。
senses.why: Like many action nouns in -ation, the word can name the doing as well as the thing done.
senses.whyCN: 与许多以 -ation 结尾的动作名词一样，这个词既能指所做的事，也能指做这件事的行为。

senses.title: A charge known to be false
senses.definition: a charge the maker knows to be untrue, as in libel and defamation cases
senses.definitionCN: 提出者明知不实的指控，常见于诽谤案件
senses.example: The court found that the allegation had been invented to damage her career.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定这项指控是为损害她的事业而编造的。
senses.why: The noun itself stays neutral, so courts must add words such as false or malicious to mark a deliberate untruth.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词本身是中性的，因此法院要另加「不实」「恶意」这类修饰语，才能标明是刻意的不实。

senses.title: A complaint inside an organisation
senses.definition: a formal complaint about a colleague's conduct, handled by an employer
senses.definitionCN: 由雇主处理、针对同事行为的正式投诉
senses.example: Human resources opened a file on the allegation before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 听证之前，人力资源部门已经为这项投诉立了档。
senses.why: Workplace procedure borrowed the legal noun for claims that never reach a court.
senses.whyCN: 职场程序借用了这个法律名词，用来指那些根本不会进法庭的说法。

senses.title: A charge still under inquiry
senses.titleCN: 调查阶段尚待核实的指控
senses.definition: a charge that is being examined and has neither been proved nor dismissed
senses.definitionCN: 正在核查、既未证实也未排除的指控
senses.example: The commission treated the allegation as pending until the emails were recovered.
senses.exampleCN: 在邮件被恢复之前，委员会把这项指控视为待定。
senses.why: Because the noun marks a claim rather than a finding, it naturally fits the period before a verdict.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词标的是「说法」而不是「认定」，它自然适用于裁决之前的那段时间。

intro.en: Allegation comes from Latin allegatio 'a bringing forward, adducing', from allegare, built on ad- 'to' and legare 'to send, depute'. It entered English through Old French in the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: allegation 来自拉丁 allegatio「提出、援引」，出自 allegare，由 ad-「朝向」与 legare「派出、委派」构成，十四世纪经古法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Legare meant 'to send as a deputy, to bequeath'; it also gives legate, legacy and legation, and has nothing to do with law as a root.
items.cn: legare 意为「作为代表派出、遗赠」；它还衍生 legate、legacy 与 legation，作为词根与「法律」无关。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus legare produced allegare 'to send forward, bring forward, adduce as evidence'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 legare 构成 allegare「往前送出、提出、作为证据援引」。

items.en: Old French allegation carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in pleadings.
items.cn: 古法语 allegation 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初用于诉状。

items.en: In early modern procedure an allegation was a statement of facts that the pleader undertook to prove.
items.cn: 在近代早期的诉讼程序中，allegation 指陈述人承诺加以证明的事实主张。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun spread to general reporting, where it now almost always signals an unproved charge.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个名词扩展到一般报道，如今几乎总是暗示指控尚未证实。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link of legare to the root of legere 'to gather, choose' is generally thought but not demonstrated; the exact first English citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：一般认为 legare 与 legere「收集、挑选」的词根有关，但未获证实；英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes whose roots are often confused with the root of allegation; group two holds the words most often used as its synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词，其词根常与 allegation 的词根混淆；第二组是最常被当作同义词使用的词。

entries.definition: From ligare 'to bind', not legare: it names loyalty owed to a ruler or a state.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ligare「捆绑」而非 legare：指对君主或国家所负的忠诚。

entries.definition: From legare 'to send as a deputy': a diplomatic mission and its staff, not a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「作为代表派出」：指外交使团及其人员，与指控无关。

entries.definition: From legare in its bequest sense: property or effects handed down by a will.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare 的遗赠义：依遗嘱传下的财产或影响。

entries.definition: From Greek allegoria 'speaking otherwise', with no connection to legare.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 allegoria「换个说法」，与 legare 没有关系。

entries.definition: The noun of accuse; it can be spoken openly and does not by itself suggest that proof is missing.
entries.definitionCN: accuse 的名词，可以公开说出，本身并不暗示缺少证据。

entries.definition: A statement that something is true, with no hint of wrongdoing unless the context supplies one.
entries.definitionCN: 断言某事为真，除非语境补充，否则不含违法意味。

entries.definition: A formal accusation in law, usually backed by an official decision to proceed.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上的正式控告，通常有官方决定推进程序作支撑。

entries.definition: A formal statement that one has been wronged, common in consumer and workplace settings.
entries.definitionCN: 正式陈述自己受了委屈，常见于消费与职场语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus legare 'send': something sent forward for others to examine.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 legare「送出」：被送到别人面前待查的东西。

normal.en: The family runs allege, allegation, alleged, allegedly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 allege、allegation、alleged 与 allegedly。

normal.en: Reporters write of allegations of fraud, never of proofs of fraud, until a finding is made.
normal.cn: 在调查结论出来之前，报道只说「欺诈指控」，不说「欺诈证据」。

normal.en: The plural is the workhorse: allegations against a company, allegations of misconduct.
normal.cn: 复数形式最常用：针对某公司的多项指控、多项不当行为指控。

normal.en: Allegiance looks close but comes from binding, not from sending.
normal.cn: allegiance 看起来相近，但它来自「捆绑」，不是「送出」。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope marked urgent but still unopened.
abstract.cn: 想象一只标着紧急却仍未拆开的信封。

abstract.en: Picture a claim standing in the middle of a room, waiting for someone to bring proof to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个说法站在房间中央，等着有人把证据搬过来。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow shaped like a person, cast by something that may not be there.
abstract.cn: 想象一个像人形的影子，投下它的东西也许并不存在。

examples.en: The company denied every allegation in the report.
examples.cn: 公司否认了报告中的每一项指控。

examples.en: Allegations of price fixing led to a formal investigation.
examples.cn: 有关操纵价格的指控引出了正式调查。

examples.en: She asked for the allegation to be put in writing before she answered it.
examples.cn: 她要求在答复之前把这项指称写成书面材料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a + leg（送出）+ ation」——把话送到别人面前，还没证实：指控、指称

root: 拉丁 allegatio「提出、援引」= ad-（朝向）+ legare「派出、送出」；legare 与 legere「收集、挑选」的联系一般认为存在，但未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle one object: a claim that has been brought forward but not yet proved, whether it sits in a pleading, a newspaper, a human resources file or a pending inquiry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个对象：一个已被提出、尚未证实的说法，它可能在诉状里、报纸上、人事档案中，也可能停在待查阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unstamped sheet of accusations pushed to the middle of the table, waiting for someone to check it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页还没盖章的控诉纸被推到桌子中央，等着有人去核实。

branches.en: THE CHARGE ITSELF: a claim of wrongdoing is brought forward before any proof exists.
branches.cn: 指控本身：在证据出现之前，违法或不当行为的说法已被提出。

branches.en: WHERE IT IS SPOKEN: the same claim can be a pleading in court or a bare assertion in debate.
branches.cn: 说在哪里：同一个说法可以是法庭上的诉状主张，也可以是争论中的单纯断言。

branches.en: HOW IT COMES: charges arrive in bundles, and the bringing of them is itself an act.
branches.cn: 如何到来：指控成批出现，而提出这一动作本身也是一件事。

branches.en: WHEN IT IS INVENTED: a charge known to be untrue turns the noun into the centre of a libel case.
branches.cn: 当它是编造的：明知不实的指控使这个名词成为诽谤案的核心。

branches.en: WHERE IT WAITS: a workplace file and a pending inquiry both hold claims that no court has judged.
branches.cn: 它在哪里等待：人事档案与待查程序都装着尚未经法院判断的说法。

intro.en: Allegation is a Latin action noun whose prefix, root and suffix each also build other English words.
intro.cn: allegation 是一个拉丁动作名词，前缀、词根与后缀各自还构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legare gives legate, legacy and legation; allegare adds direction and produces allege and allegation. Allegiance, from ligare 'to bind', belongs to a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legare 衍生 legate、legacy 与 legation；allegare 加上方向义，产生 allege 与 allegation。allegiance 来自 ligare「捆绑」，属于另一个词族。

items.structure: ad- (Latin prefix, assimilated to al- before l)
items.example: The prefix sends the claim forward into public view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把说法向前推到公众面前。

items.example: The root contributes the idea of sending something forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带来「把东西送出去」的意思。

items.meaning: to bring forward as a claim
items.example: The report alleges that the files were altered.
items.exampleCN: 报告指称这些档案被改动过。

items.example: The allegation remains unproved.
items.exampleCN: 这项指控仍未得到证实。

items.example: The alleged leak came from a former clerk.
items.exampleCN: 被指称的泄漏来自一名前职员。

items.example: He allegedly signed the order twice.
items.exampleCN: 据称他把订单签了两次。

items.example: The legation moved to a smaller building.
items.exampleCN: 公使馆搬进了一栋较小的楼。

items.example: The library was her legacy.
items.exampleCN: 这座图书馆是她留下的遗产。

definition_zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言；援引作为理由
definition_en: to state that something is true or that someone did something wrong, without proof
core_image: 一个人在文件页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的事推到桌面上
scene: 调查员把一份手写材料放进档案袋，说明材料里提到的细节还没有核实。The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
sceneCN: 这里 allege 指提出尚未证实的说法（第 1 个义项：断言某事为真而尚未举证）；句意为投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。图中可辨识物件：投诉表、档案袋、手写便条、签字笔。

pos.zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言
（法律）援引、引证作为理由或依据

senses.title: State something as true
senses.titleCN: 指称某事为真，尚未举证
senses.definition: to state that something is the case without offering proof
senses.definitionCN: 断言某事确实如此，但未提供证据
senses.example: The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
senses.exampleCN: 投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。
senses.why: Latin allegare meant 'to bring forward, adduce'; a claim is brought forward before the proof that would support it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 allegare 意为「提出、援引」；说法先被提出，支持它的证据后才可能到来。

senses.title: State it in a pleading
senses.titleCN: 在诉状或正式文书中陈述
senses.definition: to set out a fact as true in a legal or official document
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或官方文书中把某项事实陈述为真
senses.example: The plaintiff alleges that the contract was signed under duress.
senses.exampleCN: 原告主张合同是在胁迫下签署的。
senses.why: In pleadings the verb marks a fact the party undertakes to prove, so the legal sense keeps its forward-looking force.
senses.whyCN: 在诉状中，这个动词标出一项当事人承诺日后证明的事实，因此法律义保留了「向前提出」的劲头。

senses.title: Name a person's act
senses.definition: to say that a named person performed a particular act
senses.definitionCN: 指认某个具体的人做过某件具体的事
senses.example: The article alleges that two officials took payments from the contractor.
senses.exampleCN: 文章指称两名官员收受了承包商的款项。
senses.why: The pattern allege that someone did something lets a newspaper name the act while leaving the proof to others.
senses.whyCN: 「指称某人做过某事」这一结构让报纸点明行为，同时把举证留给别人。

senses.title: Cite as a reason
senses.definition: to offer something as a reason, excuse or justification
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物作为理由、借口或正当依据提出
senses.example: He alleged pressure from his superiors as the reason for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他称上级施加的压力是延误的原因。
senses.why: Adducing a reason is literally bringing something forward, so the same verb serves for excuses and justifications.
senses.whyCN: 提供理由字面上就是把某物提出来，因此同一个动词也能用于借口与辩解。

senses.title: Cite a precedent or text
senses.definition: to quote a case, a rule or a passage in support of an argument
senses.definitionCN: 为支持论点而援引案例、规则或文句
senses.example: Counsel alleged two earlier rulings in support of the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 律师援引了先前两份裁决来支持这一主张。
senses.why: A precedent is also brought forward into an argument, and the old sense of adducing survives in this usage.
senses.whyCN: 先例同样是被提出来放进论证，于是「援引」的旧义在这一用法中留存。

senses.title: Plead in excuse
senses.definition: to plead something as an excuse, an older sense now largely confined to legal and literary texts
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作辩解提出，这一旧义如今多限于法律与文学文本
senses.example: In the old account he alleged illness and left the assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的记述里，他称病离开了集会。
senses.why: The older sense of adducing a defence survives in legal phrasing, where a party alleges facts to escape liability.
senses.whyCN: 「提出抗辩」的旧义残留在法律措辞里：一方援引事实以摆脱责任。

senses.title: The alleged offender
senses.titleCN: 分词形容词：被指称的，涉嫌的
senses.definition: alleged, as an adjective: named in a claim but not proved guilty
senses.definitionCN: alleged 作形容词：被指称但尚未证实有罪的
senses.example: The alleged offender was never charged.
senses.exampleCN: 被指称的涉案人从未被起诉。
senses.why: The past participle marks a person named in a claim but not yet tried, which is exactly the gap the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词标记「被指称却尚未受审」的人，正好对应这个动词所描述的缺口。

senses.title: The reported claim
senses.titleCN: 被动与副词形式：据称、据悉
senses.definition: be alleged to and allegedly: forms that report a claim while keeping the speaker at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 这类转述形式把说法归到他人名下，同时让说话者保持距离
senses.example: The firm is alleged to have moved the money offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 据称该公司把钱转移到了海外。
senses.why: Reported forms are the safest way for a paper to repeat a charge it cannot prove.
senses.whyCN: 对无法举证的指控，转述形式是报纸最稳妥的表达方式。

intro.en: Allege comes through Anglo-French aleger from Latin allegare 'to send forward, adduce', built on ad- 'to' and legare 'to send, depute'. It entered English in the fourteenth century as a pleading verb. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 来自拉丁 allegare「向前送出、援引」，由 ad-「朝向」与 legare「派出、委派」构成，十四世纪作为诉讼用语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Legare meant 'to send as a deputy' and also 'to bequeath'; the root has no connection with law.
items.cn: legare 意为「作为代表派出」，也有「遗赠」义；这个词根与「法律」无关。

items.en: Ad- plus legare gave allegare 'to bring forward, adduce, plead as evidence'.
items.cn: ad- 加 legare 构成 allegare「向前提出、援引、作为证据陈说」。

items.en: Anglo-French aleger carried the legal verb into English courts in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—法语 aleger 在十四世纪把这个法律动词带入英格兰的法庭。

items.en: In pleading, to allege was to state a fact that the party undertook to prove later.
items.cn: 在诉讼中，allege 指陈述一项当事人承诺日后加以证明的事实。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb was used outside court for any claim put forward without proof, and the passive became the reporter's default.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词在法庭之外用于任何未经证实而提出的说法，被动式则成了报道的默认写法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the tie between legare and the root of legere 'to gather, choose' is generally thought but not proved; first records are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：一般认为 legare 与 legere「收集、挑选」的词根有关，但未获证实；最早书证为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that share letters or a look with allege but not its root; group two holds verbs of asserting, ranked by how much proof they imply.
note.cn: 第一组是字母或外形与 allege 相近、却不同源的词；第二组是断言类动词，按所含证据分量排列。

entries.definition: From ligare 'to bind', so it means loyalty owed, not a claim made.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ligare「捆绑」，指所负的忠诚，而不是提出的说法。

entries.definition: From legare 'bequeath': what a will or a past age leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「遗赠」：遗嘱或过往时代留下的东西。

entries.definition: From legare 'send as a deputy': an official envoy, especially a papal one.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「作为代表派出」：官方使节，尤指教廷使节。

entries.definition: From Greek allegoria 'speaking otherwise'; a story carrying a second meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 allegoria「换个说法」：承载第二层含义的故事。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for saying something is true, with no suggestion that proof is missing.
entries.definitionCN: 说某事为真的日常动词，不暗示缺少证据。

entries.definition: To state something confidently; it stresses the speaker's conviction rather than the lack of proof.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地陈述某事，强调说话者的确信，而非缺少证据。

entries.definition: To say someone did wrong; it always targets a person or body, while allege often targets a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人做错事，总有一个被指对象；而 allege 常指向一件事实。

entries.definition: To argue that something is true as part of a dispute, implying opposing views.
entries.definitionCN: 在争论中主张某事为真，暗示存在对立观点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus legare 'send': a claim sent forward for others to test.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 legare「送」：把说法送到别人面前去检验。

normal.en: The family runs allege, allegation, alleged, allegedly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 allege、allegation、alleged 与 allegedly。

normal.en: News prose prefers the passive: the company is alleged to have...
normal.cn: 新闻语体偏爱被动式：据称该公司曾……

normal.en: A pleading alleges facts; the other side then admits or denies them.
normal.cn: 诉状提出事实主张，随后由对方承认或否认。

normal.en: Allegiance is a false friend from the binding root, not from sending.
normal.cn: allegiance 是假朋友，来自「捆绑」的词根，与「送出」无关。

abstract.en: Picture a claim pushed through a door before anyone checks who is behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个说法被推进门里，却没人先确认门后是谁。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the foot of a page that nobody has read to the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一页没人读完的文件，页脚已经有了签名。

abstract.en: Picture a label reading reported stuck to a parcel nobody has opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一只贴着「据报」标签、却没人拆开过的包裹。

examples.en: The study alleges a link between the two chemicals and the illness.
examples.cn: 这项研究称这两种化学品与那种疾病存在关联。

examples.en: It was alleged that the files had been destroyed before the hearing.
examples.cn: 据称档案在听证之前就已被销毁。

examples.en: She alleged no reason for the delay and simply left.
examples.cn: 她没有给出延误的任何理由，就此离开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a + lege（送出）」——话先送出去，证据后再补：指称、声称

root: 拉丁 allegare「向前提出、援引」= ad-（朝向）+ legare「派出、送出」；英语 allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one move: a claim is sent forward, then the settings change from court to newspaper to quotation, and finally to the grammatical forms that report it at arm's length.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：说法先被送出去，接着场景从法庭换到报纸再到引证，最后落在把那项说法隔开距离转述的语法形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone signs the word reported at the foot of a page and pushes the unverified sheet across the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人在页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的纸推到桌子对面。

branches.en: THE CLAIM SENT: the same move serves a newspaper sentence and a formal pleading.
branches.cn: 送出的说法：同一个动作既用于报纸句子，也用于正式诉状。

branches.en: THE ACT NAMED: a person and a deed are specified, while the proof stays elsewhere.
branches.cn: 点明的行为：指出具体的人与具体的事，证据却留在别处。

branches.en: THE REASON ADDUCED: a pressure, a precedent or a passage is brought forward in support.
branches.cn: 援引的理由：把压力、先例或文句提出来充当依据。

branches.en: THE OLD DEFENCE: pleading illness or some other fact to escape a duty belongs to an older legal idiom.
branches.cn: 古老的辩解：称病或以其他事实脱责，属于更早的法律习语。

branches.en: THE REPORTED FORM: the participle and the adverb let a writer repeat a charge without owning it.
branches.cn: 转述形式：分词与副词让写作者重复一项指控，却不必替它担保。

intro.en: Allege is a Latin verb whose prefix, root and suffixes each build other English words.
intro.cn: allege 是一个拉丁动词，前缀、词根与后缀各自还构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legare gives legate, legacy and legation; allege and allegation come from allegare, where ad- adds direction. Allegiance belongs to the binding root and not here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legare 衍生 legate、legacy 与 legation；allege 与 allegation 出自 allegare，由 ad- 增添方向义。allegiance 属于「捆绑」词根，不在这一族。

items.example: The prefix pushes the claim into view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把说法推到人前。

items.example: The root supplies the sending.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「送出」的意思。

items.meaning: to bring forward as a claim
items.example: The report alleges that the forms were altered.
items.exampleCN: 报告指称这些表格被改动过。

items.example: The allegation was later withdrawn.
items.exampleCN: 这项指控后来被撤回。

items.example: The alleged theft was never reported.
items.exampleCN: 被指称的盗窃从未有人报案。

items.example: The clerk allegedly deleted the file.
items.exampleCN: 据称那名职员删除了文件。

items.example: The legation closed in the spring.
items.exampleCN: 那个公使馆在春天关闭了。

items.example: The legate carried a sealed letter.
items.exampleCN: 使节带着一封密封的信。

definition_zh: 证据；证明材料；迹象；（少见，动词）表明、证实
definition_en: facts, objects or statements that show something is true or that prove what happened
core_image: 一只透明封袋装着指纹卡片、照片与笔录，被放到法庭的木桌上
scene: 鉴证人员把封好的透明袋放在桌上，袋里的纤维与照片都贴着编号标签。The sealed bag of fibres was submitted as evidence.
sceneCN: 这里 evidence 指用来证明事实的材料（第 1 个义项：证明某事实为真的材料或物品）；句意为装有纤维的封袋被作为证据提交。图中可辨识物件：透明封袋、编号标签、照片、法官的木槌。

pos.zh: 证据；证明材料；迹象（不可数）
表明；证实（少见，多见于书面语）

senses.title: Material that proves a fact
senses.definition: facts, objects or statements that show something to be true
senses.definitionCN: 显示某事为真的事实、物品或陈述
senses.example: The sealed bag of fibres was submitted as evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 装有纤维的封袋被作为证据提交。
senses.why: Latin evidentia meant 'clearness': what is evident is what can be seen out in the open, and evidence is the thing that makes a fact visible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 evidentia 意为「清楚」：evident 指可以当众看见的，而 evidence 就是使事实可见的东西。

senses.title: A sign or trace
senses.definition: an indication that something exists or has happened
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事物存在或发生过的痕迹
senses.example: The worn steps are evidence that the stair was used daily.
senses.exampleCN: 被磨薄的台阶说明这道楼梯每天都被使用。
senses.why: A trace makes an unseen event visible after the fact, which is the same gesture as proof at a smaller scale.
senses.whyCN: 痕迹在事后让看不见的事件变得可见，这与「证明」是同一动作的缩小版。

senses.title: Sworn words in court
senses.definition: the statements of witnesses given under oath in a legal proceeding
senses.definitionCN: 证人在法律程序中宣誓后作出的陈述
senses.example: The jury weighed the evidence of three witnesses against the video.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团把三名证人的证词与录像对照衡量。
senses.why: In court, spoken testimony is itself a form of evidence, so the word covers words as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，口头证词本身就是一种证据，因此这个词既指物品也指言辞。

senses.title: Objects examined in court
senses.definition: physical items produced in a case, such as weapons, samples or documents
senses.definitionCN: 案件中出示的实物，如器物、样本或文件
senses.example: The lab kept the physical evidence in a locked cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把物证锁在柜子里。
senses.why: Forensic practice separates objects from words, and physical evidence names the object half.
senses.whyCN: 法庭科学把实物与言辞分开，物证这一说法专指实物那一半。

senses.title: Proof by inference
senses.definition: proof that works by inference rather than direct observation
senses.definitionCN: 通过推论而非直接观察成立的证明
senses.example: No one saw the break-in, so the case rested on circumstantial evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人看到入侵过程，案子只能依靠间接证据。
senses.why: Evidence need not be seen directly; a chain of small facts can make a conclusion visible.
senses.whyCN: 证据不必被直接看到；一串细小事实同样能让结论变得可见。

senses.title: To show or indicate
senses.definition: to show or indicate something, usually of a thing rather than a person
senses.definitionCN: 表明或显示某事，主语多为事物而非人
senses.example: The cracked wall evidenced years of settling.
senses.exampleCN: 开裂的墙面表明地基多年下沉。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of being the proof, the thing now does the showing.
senses.whyCN: 动词用法把名词关系倒过来：事物不再是证据，而是发出显示的一方。

senses.title: Being on display
senses.titleCN: 显眼、被展示出来的状态
senses.definition: in evidence: visible and prominent, especially in a public setting
senses.definitionCN: 在「作为证据出示、引人注目」这一固定说法里，指显眼、惹人注意，多用于公共场合
senses.example: Her calm manner was in evidence throughout the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 整场听证中，她的镇定一直显而易见。
senses.why: The old phrase in evidence keeps the Latin sense of clearness and moves it from proof to visibility.
senses.whyCN: 「作为证据出示」这一旧说法保留了拉丁语「清楚」的含义，并从「证明」转向「可见」。

senses.title: The body of proof in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域积累的证据总量
senses.definition: the accumulated body of findings that a field relies on
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科赖以立论的既有研究发现总和
senses.example: The evidence base for the treatment is still thin.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疗法的证据基础仍然薄弱。
senses.why: Research talk turns countable findings into an uncountable mass, and evidence becomes a body rather than a bag.
senses.whyCN: 研究语境把可数的发现汇成不可数的总量，evidence 于是从一袋东西变成一整个体系。

intro.en: Evidence comes through Old French from Latin evidentia 'clearness, distinctness', from evidens, built on e- 'out' and videre 'to see'. The legal sense developed in English in the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: evidence 经古法语来自拉丁 evidentia「清楚、分明」，出自 evidens，由 e-「向外」与 videre「看见」构成。法律义在十四世纪的英语中发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Videre meant 'to see'; its deeper root is reconstructed as a form meaning 'to see, to know', and the reconstruction is not a recorded word.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」；其更深的词根被重构为表示「看见、知晓」的形式，该形式并非有记录的词。

items.en: E- 'out' plus videre produced evidens 'visible, clear', literally 'that can be seen out'.
items.cn: e-「向外」加 videre 构成 evidens「可见的、清楚的」，字面是「能看出来」。

items.en: Evidentia named the quality of being clear; it did not yet mean proof material.
items.cn: evidentia 指「清楚」这一性质，当时还没有「证明材料」的意思。

items.en: Old French evidence carried the word into English, where it first described obviousness.
items.cn: 古法语 evidence 把这个词带入英语，最初表示「显而易见」。

items.en: By the fifteenth century evidence named testimony and documents in a case; the scientific sense of accumulated findings followed much later.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，evidence 已指案件中的证词与文件；研究意义上的「累积发现」则晚得多。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin root of videre is a reconstruction, and the exact first legal citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：videre 在拉丁语之前的词根属于重构形式，法律义最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on videre or on a look-alike stem; group two holds the nouns and objects that a case is built from.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 videre 或形似的词干；第二组是构成一桩案件的各种证明材料与相应名词。

entries.definition: The adjective of the same family: clear to the eye or mind, without the sense of a proof item.
entries.definitionCN: 同族形容词：对眼睛或心智而言清楚，不含「证明材料」的意思。

entries.definition: From evincere, built on vincere 'to conquer': to show a quality by one's behaviour, not to supply proof.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 evincere，词根是 vincere「征服」：以行为显出某种品质，而不是提供证据。

entries.definition: Pro- 'before' plus videre: seeing ahead, hence foresight and care.
entries.definitionCN: pro-「在前」加 videre：预先看见，因此指远见与照护。

entries.definition: Latin for 'I see', the first-person form of the same verb, now an English noun for recorded pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「我看见」，正是同一个动词的第一人称形式，如今作英语名词指录像。

entries.definition: Proof is what evidence produces; a proof settles a question, while evidence may still be disputed.
entries.definitionCN: proof 是证据产生的结果：证明能了结问题，证据本身仍可能有争议。

entries.definition: Statements made by witnesses, especially under oath; it is one kind of evidence, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 证人在庭上尤其宣誓后作出的陈述，是证据的一种而非全部。

entries.definition: A physical item formally shown in court and labelled for the record.
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上正式出示并编入卷宗的实物。

entries.definition: A small fact that points toward an answer; it guides an inquiry rather than concluding it.
entries.definitionCN: 指向答案的小事实，只引导调查，不作结论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: E- 'out' plus videre 'see': what can be seen out in the open.
normal.cn: e-「向外」加 videre「看见」：能当众看出来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs evidence, evident, evidential, evidently, evidence-based.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evidence、evident、evidential、evidently 与 evidence-based。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the field: physical evidence, circumstantial evidence, admissible evidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配切分了这个领域：物证、间接证据、可采信证据。

normal.en: Courts say give evidence, and laboratories say the evidence shows.
normal.cn: 法庭上说「提供证据」，实验室里说「证据显示」。

normal.en: Evince looks close but comes from conquering, not from seeing.
normal.cn: evince 看似相近，却来自「征服」而非「看见」。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switched on inside a dark room: the room was always there, but only now is it visible.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里打开一盏灯：房间一直在那里，只是此刻才变得可见。

abstract.en: Picture footprints in fresh snow that keep walking after the walker has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象新雪上的脚印，走路的人已经离开，脚印还在往前延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom table where objects and words sit side by side as equal witnesses.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭的木桌旁，实物与言辞并排而坐，同样是证人。

examples.en: The survey offers little evidence that the policy changed behaviour.
examples.cn: 这项调查几乎没有提供证据说明该政策改变了行为。

examples.en: Her hands showed evidence of long work in the cold.
examples.cn: 她的双手留有在寒地里长期劳作的痕迹。

examples.en: The defence argued that the video was not admissible as evidence.
examples.cn: 辩方主张该录像不能作为证据采信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（外）+ vid（看）+ ence」——把事实摆出来让人看见：证据

root: 拉丁 evidentia「清楚」= e-（向外）+ videre「看见」；videre 更深词根为重构形式，英语 evidence 经古法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from things that are seen to things that are shown: a proof item, a trace, spoken words, an object, an inference, a verb, a state of visibility and a whole body of findings.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「被看见」走向「被显示」：证明材料、痕迹、言辞、实物、推论、动词用法、显眼状态，最后是一整个证据体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear bag of objects and papers set on a courtroom table where everyone can see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只透明的袋子装着实物与纸页，摆在人人都能看见的法庭木桌上。

branches.en: WHAT SHOWS: a proof item and a small trace both make an unseen fact visible.
branches.cn: 显示之物：证明材料与细小痕迹都在让看不见的事实变得可见。

branches.en: WORDS AS PROOF: sworn statements count as evidence, so speech joins the objects.
branches.cn: 言辞作证：宣誓后的陈述也算证据，于是言辞与实物并列。

branches.en: THINGS AND LINKS: one item is shown in court, while a chain of items can carry a conclusion.
branches.cn: 实物与链条：一件东西在法庭上出示，一串东西也能撑起一个结论。

branches.en: THE VERB AND THE PHRASE: the thing that proves can itself show, and evidence can mean simply being visible.
branches.cn: 动词与短语：能作证的东西本身也能显示，而 evidence 还可以只指「显眼」。

branches.en: THE WHOLE STORE: a field gathers its scattered findings into one evidence base.
branches.cn: 整体储备：一个学科把散落的发现汇成一份证据基础。

intro.en: Evidence is a Latin noun whose prefix and root still build a visible family in English.
intro.cn: evidence 是一个拉丁名词，其前缀与词根在英语中仍构成一个可见的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre gives vision, video, evident and evidence; e- adds the sense of something coming out into view.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 衍生 vision、video、evident 与 evidence；e- 增添「显现出来」的意思。

items.example: The prefix pulls the fact out of hiding.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把事实从隐蔽处拉出来。

items.example: The root carries the act of seeing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「看见」这个动作。

items.example: The answer was evident to everyone.
items.exampleCN: 答案对每个人都显而易见。

items.meaning: the state of being clear, then a proof item
items.meaningCN: 清楚的状态，后指证明材料
items.example: The fibres were kept as evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这些纤维被留作证据。

items.example: The note has evidential value.
items.exampleCN: 这份记录具有证据价值。

items.meaning: in a way that is clear
items.example: She was evidently unprepared.
items.exampleCN: 她显然没有准备。

items.meaning: relating to the rules of proof
items.meaningCN: 证据规则的；用于举证的
items.example: The judge applied the evidentiary standard.
items.exampleCN: 法官适用了证据标准。

items.example: Her calm was in evidence all morning.
items.exampleCN: 整个上午她的镇定都很明显。

definition_zh: 证据的；可作证据的；证据性的；（语言学）示证的
definition_en: relating to evidence, or able to serve as evidence
core_image: 一叠贴着编号的证据袋被摊开，旁边白板上画着信息来源的推断路径
scene: 语言学家在白板上画出信息来源的标记，说明有些语言用专门词尾交代消息从哪来。Some languages mark evidential meaning with a suffix.
sceneCN: 这里 evidential 指与证据来源有关的（第 1 个义项：与证据相关的、属于证据范畴的）；句意为有些语言用后缀标示示证意义。图中可辨识物件：白板、词尾卡片、箭头、声波图。

pos.zh: 证据的；可作证据的；证据性的
（语言学）示证的；标示信息来源的

senses.title: Relating to evidence
senses.definition: relating to evidence in general, especially in legal and scientific settings
senses.definitionCN: 与证据有关，多用于法律与研究语境
senses.example: The note has evidential value for the historian.
senses.exampleCN: 这份记录对史学家具有证据价值。
senses.why: Evidential is evidence plus the adjective suffix -al, so it names the whole class of things that have to do with proof.
senses.whyCN: evidential 是 evidence 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，因此指一切与证明有关的属性。

senses.title: Usable as evidence
senses.definition: able to be used as evidence in a case or an inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 可在案件或调查中作为证据使用
senses.example: Only the signed sheets were evidential; the drafts were not.
senses.exampleCN: 只有签过字的纸张才算证据，草稿不算。
senses.why: The suffix turns a broad relation into a qualification: a thing becomes evidential when a rule allows it into the record.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀把宽泛的关联变成一种资格：当规则允许某物进入案卷时，它就成其为证据性材料。

senses.title: Reasoning from proof
senses.definition: based on evidence rather than on assumption or authority
senses.definitionCN: 依据证据而非假设或权威进行的
senses.example: Evidential reasoning asks what the traces would look like if each hypothesis were true.
senses.exampleCN: 依据证据的推理会追问：若各个假设成立，痕迹会是什么样。
senses.why: Once proof items exist they can be weighed against competing accounts, and the adjective attaches to the method rather than the item.
senses.whyCN: 证据一旦存在，就能与不同说法相互衡量，这个形容词于是附着在方法上，而不是某件材料上。

senses.title: The linguistic category
senses.definition: marking how the speaker knows something, as through sight, hearsay or inference
senses.definitionCN: 标示说话者如何得知某事的语法范畴，如亲见、传闻或推断
senses.example: Some languages mark evidential meaning with a suffix.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言用后缀标示示证意义。
senses.why: Linguists borrowed the adjective for grammar because a suffix can state the source of the speaker's evidence.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把这一形容词借到语法领域，因为一个后缀就能交代说话者证据的来源。

senses.title: The burden in litigation
senses.definition: the evidential burden: the duty to produce enough proof for a matter to be considered
senses.definitionCN: 在「举证负担」这一术语中，指为使某一争点进入审理而须提出足够证据的责任
senses.example: The evidential burden shifts once the defence raises the alibi.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提出不在场证明后，举证负担随之转移。
senses.why: Procedure separates the duty to persuade from the duty to bring proof, and this adjective marks the narrower one.
senses.whyCN: 程序法把「说服责任」与「提出证据的责任」分开，这个形容词标的是较窄的那一种。

senses.title: Weight in assessment
senses.definition: the strength that a piece of proof carries when findings are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较各项结论时某份材料所具有的证明力度
senses.example: The two studies carry different evidential weight.
senses.exampleCN: 这两项研究的证据分量不同。
senses.why: Once proof items are weighed rather than merely listed, the adjective moves from kind to degree.
senses.whyCN: 当证据不只是被列出、而是被衡量时，这个形容词就从「类别」转向「程度」。

senses.title: Indicative of something
senses.titleCN: 表明某种迹象的（旧用法）
senses.definition: serving as a sign of something, an older sense close to indicative
senses.definitionCN: 充当某事物的迹象，这一旧义接近 indicative
senses.example: A steady pulse was evidential of recovery in the old medical texts.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧医学文本里，平稳的脉搏是康复的迹象。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is visibility, so anything that makes a condition visible can still be called evidential.
senses.whyCN: 词根最古老的意思是「可见」，因此凡能让某种状况变得可见的东西仍可称为 evidential。

senses.title: Of physical proof in forensics
senses.titleCN: 法庭科学中的物证属性
senses.definition: relating to physical items handled as proof in forensic work
senses.definitionCN: 与法庭科学中作为证据处理的实物有关
senses.example: The evidential material was dried before it was packed.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据材料在封装前先被晾干。
senses.why: Forensic labs use the adjective for the physical half of a case, the objects that can be measured and sealed.
senses.whyCN: 法庭实验室用这个形容词指案件中的实物那一半，即可以测量与封存的东西。

intro.en: Evidential is formed inside English from evidence plus the adjective suffix -al, and is recorded from the nineteenth century. Evidence itself comes from Latin evidentia 'clearness', built on e- 'out' and videre 'to see'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: evidential 是在英语内部由 evidence 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，十九世纪起有记录。evidence 本身来自拉丁 evidentia「清楚」，由 e-「向外」与 videre「看见」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Evidentia named clearness or distinctness, from evidens 'visible, clear'.
items.cn: evidentia 指清楚、分明，出自 evidens「可见的、清楚的」。

items.en: English evidence first meant obviousness and later the material that makes a fact clear.
items.cn: 英语 evidence 最初指显而易见，后来指使事实变得清楚的材料。

items.en: -al, from Latin -alis, forms adjectives meaning 'relating to'; attached to evidence it yields evidential.
items.cn: -al 出自拉丁 -alis，构成表示「与……有关」的形容词；加在 evidence 上就得到 evidential。

items.en: The adjective spread in legal and philosophical writing, where proof and the testing of proof were being separated.
items.cn: 这个形容词在法律与哲学写作中流传开来，当时人们正把「证明」与「对证明的检验」区分开来。

items.en: In the twentieth century linguists applied it to grammatical markers of the source of knowledge, and the noun evidentiality followed.
items.cn: 二十世纪语言学家把它用于标示知识来源的语法标记，随后出现了名词 evidentiality。

items.en: The chain evidence plus -al is clear; only the exact year of the earliest citation is uncertain, so the adjective is dated to the nineteenth century as an approximation.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：evidence 加 -al 这条词源链清楚，只有最早书证的确切年份不确定，因此把形容词的首见年代按十九世纪作为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same family and one false friend; group two holds adjectives that also speak about proof but from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族成员与一个假朋友；第二组是同样谈论证明、但角度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: Means clear or obvious; it describes the fact, while evidential describes the proof of the fact.
entries.definitionCN: 意为明显、清楚；它描述事实本身，evidential 描述证明该事实的材料。

entries.definition: The adverb of evident, used for conclusions the speaker draws, not for rules about proof.
entries.definitionCN: evident 的副词，用于说话者自己得出的结论，而不是关于证据的规则。

entries.definition: From evincere, built on vincere 'to conquer': to display a quality, not to relate to evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 evincere，词根是 vincere「征服」：显出某种品质，与「证据」无关。

entries.definition: The grammatical category itself, formed from evidential plus -ity; the adjective names what the noun studies.
entries.definitionCN: 指示证这一语法范畴本身，由 evidential 加 -ity 构成；形容词指该范畴所修饰的东西。

entries.definition: From probare 'to test': having the power to prove something, a stronger claim than merely relating to proof.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 probare「检验」：具有证明力，比「与证据有关」更强。

entries.definition: Serving as a sign of something; it stops short of formal proof.
entries.definitionCN: 充当某事物的迹象，尚未达到正式证明。

entries.definition: Permitted by the rules of a court to be considered as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 依法院规则获准作为证据加以考虑。

entries.definition: From corroborare 'to strengthen': adding weight to proof that already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 corroborare「加强」：为已有证据增加分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Evidence plus -al: the adjective of proof.
normal.cn: evidence 加 -al：证据的形容词形式。

normal.en: The family runs evidence, evident, evidential, evidentiality, evidently.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evidence、evident、evidential、evidentiality 与 evidently。

normal.en: Legal usage pairs it with burden and value: evidential burden, evidential value.
normal.cn: 法律用法常与 burden、value 搭配：举证负担、证据价值。

normal.en: Linguistics pairs it with marker and system: evidential marker, evidential system.
normal.cn: 语言学常与 marker、system 搭配：示证标记、示证系统。

normal.en: Evince is a false friend from the conquering root.
normal.cn: evince 是假朋友，来自「征服」的词根。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a box stating where its contents came from.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子上贴着标签，写明里面的东西从哪来。

abstract.en: Picture a set of scales that weighs proofs instead of counting them.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，称的是证据的分量而不是件数。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence ending in a small tag that says how the speaker knows.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话末尾附着小标记，交代说话者是怎么知道的。

examples.en: The diary is evidential for the price of bread but not for the king's thoughts.
examples.cn: 这本日记对面包价格有证据价值，却不足以说明国王的想法。

examples.en: Her silence was evidential of nothing except exhaustion.
examples.cn: 她的沉默除了疲惫之外说明不了什么。

examples.en: The language marks hearsay with an evidential particle.
examples.cn: 这门语言用示证助词标示传闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evidence（证据）+ al（……的）」——关于证据的、能当证据的

root: 英语 evidence（证据）+ 形容词后缀 -al；evidence 出自拉丁 evidentia「清楚」= e-（向外）+ videre「看见」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses widen one relation: first a general tie to proof, then fitness for the record, then reasoning, a grammatical category, a procedural duty, a measured weight, an older sense of 'indicative' and the physical objects of a laboratory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把一个关系逐步撑开：先是与证据的一般关联，再是可入案的资格、依证据推理、语法范畴、程序义务、可衡量的分量、较旧的「表明」义，最后是实验室里的实物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered evidence bags laid out beside a whiteboard that traces where each item came from.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着编号的证据袋一字排开，旁边白板画出每件东西的来源路径。

branches.en: THE PROOF RELATION: the adjective ties an object to proof, then asks whether a rule lets it in.
branches.cn: 与证据的关系：先指某物与证据有关，再问规则是否允许它入案。

branches.en: REASONING: conclusions are drawn from traces rather than from authority.
branches.cn: 推理：结论取自痕迹，而不是取自权威。

branches.en: THE GRAMMATICAL MARK: a suffix states whether the speaker saw, heard or inferred the thing.
branches.cn: 语法标记：一个后缀说明说话者是亲见、听闻还是推断。

branches.en: DUTY AND WEIGHT: procedure assigns who must bring proof, and assessment asks how much it is worth.
branches.cn: 义务与分量：程序规定谁须举证，评估则问这份证据值多少。

branches.en: SIGN AND OBJECT: the older sense merely points at a sign, while forensics returns the word to sealed physical items.
branches.cn: 迹象与实物：较旧的义项只是指向迹象，法庭科学则把这个词带回封存的实物。

intro.en: Evidential is an English adjective built on evidence; both parts of the Latin source still build words in English.
intro.cn: evidential 是建立在 evidence 之上的英语形容词；其拉丁来源的两个部分在英语中仍在构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre gives vision and video, and e- 'out' shapes evident, evidence and evidential.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 衍生 vision 与 video，而 e-「向外」塑造了 evident、evidence 与 evidential。

items.example: The prefix brings the fact into view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把事实带到人眼前。

items.example: The root supplies the seeing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「看见」的意思。

items.example: The pattern was evident in the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个规律在数据中很明显。

items.example: The bags held the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 袋子里装着证据。

items.example: The letter has evidential weight.
items.exampleCN: 这封信有证据分量。

items.example: The claim was evidentially weak.
items.exampleCN: 这一主张在证据上很薄弱。

items.meaningCN: 示证性；信息来源的语法标示
items.example: Evidentiality is common in the language.
items.exampleCN: 示证性在这门语言中很常见。

items.example: The clinic follows evidence-based practice.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所采用循证做法。

definition_zh: 证词；证言；见证；（对某事的）明证
definition_en: a formal statement, especially one made under oath in court, that something is true
core_image: 证人站在庭上，手按誓词，把所见一句一句说给速记员
scene: 证人席上的人举起手，速记员开始敲下他说的每一句。Her testimony lasted nearly three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 testimony 指证人在法庭上给出的证词（第 1 个义项：法庭上作出的正式陈述）；句意为她的证词持续了将近三个小时。图中可辨识物件：证人席、速记键盘、誓词卡、记者笔记本。

pos.zh: 证词；证言（法律）
见证；明证；公开的陈述

derivatives.zh: 遗嘱；证明（同出 testari 词根）

senses.title: Sworn statement in court
senses.definition: a formal statement made under oath by a witness in a legal proceeding
senses.definitionCN: 证人在法律程序中宣誓后作出的正式陈述
senses.example: Her testimony lasted nearly three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她的证词持续了将近三个小时。
senses.why: Testimony comes from Latin testimonium, built on testis 'witness': it is the words a witness contributes to a case.
senses.whyCN: testimony 出自拉丁 testimonium，词根是 testis「证人」：它是证人为案件提供的言辞。

senses.title: Expert evidence
senses.definition: the statement of a specialist explaining technical matters to a court
senses.definitionCN: 专家向法庭解释专门问题的陈述
senses.example: The geologist's testimony turned on the age of the layer.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家的证言关键在于那一层的年代。
senses.why: A specialist is still a witness, so the word covers informed opinion as well as eyewitness fact.
senses.whyCN: 专家同样是证人，因此这个词既指亲见的事实，也指有依据的专业判断。

senses.title: Bearing witness to something
senses.definition: a public act of confirming something one has seen or known
senses.definitionCN: 公开确认自己所见所知的行为
senses.example: Her letters bear testimony to a long friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书信见证了长久的友谊。
senses.why: The old phrase bear testimony keeps the witness in view while the object shifts from a crime to a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 「作见证」这一旧说法仍保留「见证人」的意思，只是对象从罪行换成了关系。

senses.title: A clear sign of something
senses.definition: something that serves as clear proof of a quality or an event
senses.definitionCN: 作为某品质或某事件的明确证明的事物
senses.example: The rebuilt square is testimony to the city's recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 重建的广场是该城复苏的明证。
senses.why: When an object testifies, it does what a witness does: it makes a fact publicly undeniable.
senses.whyCN: 当一件物品「作证」时，它做的事与证人相同：让某项事实变得公开而无可否认。

senses.title: Written statement
senses.definition: a written statement sworn or affirmed before a person with authority
senses.definitionCN: 在有权者面前宣誓或确认的书面陈述
senses.example: The clerk read the written testimony into the record.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员把书面证词读入案卷。
senses.why: Procedure accepts words on paper as testimony, so the noun covers documents as well as speech.
senses.whyCN: 程序法承认纸面文字同样构成证词，因此这个词也指文件。

senses.title: The voices of many witnesses
senses.definition: the collected statements of several witnesses considered together
senses.definitionCN: 把若干证人的陈述合并考察
senses.example: The testimony of the passengers contradicted the driver's account.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客们的证词与司机的说法相矛盾。
senses.why: The uncountable use treats many statements as one body of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法把许多陈述当成一整份证据。

senses.title: Public declaration of faith
senses.titleCN: 宗教集会中的信仰见证
senses.definition: a personal account of religious experience given to a congregation
senses.definitionCN: 在会众面前讲述个人宗教经历的陈述
senses.example: He gave his testimony before the congregation at the spring meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他在春季聚会上向会众讲述了自己的信仰见证。
senses.why: Religious communities borrowed the legal noun for a statement whose truth rests on the speaker's own life.
senses.whyCN: 宗教群体借用了这个法律名词，用来指以讲述者自身经历为凭的陈述。

senses.title: Statement to an inquiry
senses.titleCN: 听证会或调查中的正式陈述
senses.definition: a formal statement given to a committee, commission or investigation
senses.definitionCN: 向委员会、调查组或听证会作出的正式陈述
senses.example: Her testimony before the committee was released in full.
senses.exampleCN: 她在委员会上的证词被全文公布。
senses.why: Outside a courtroom the noun still means a formal statement on oath, which is why hearings use it.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭之外，这个词仍指正式宣誓的陈述，因此听证会沿用它。

intro.en: Testimony comes through Anglo-French from Latin testimonium 'evidence, witness', built on testis 'witness' plus the noun suffix -monium. It is recorded in English from the thirteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: testimony 经盎格鲁—法语来自拉丁 testimonium「证据、见证」，由 testis「证人」加名词后缀 -monium 构成，十三世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Testis meant 'witness'. Its deeper origin is not established; the suggestion that it began as 'third person standing by' is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: testis 意为「证人」。其更深来源未获证明；认为它原指「站在一旁的第三人」的说法属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Testis plus -monium produced testimonium 'evidence, testimony, proof'.
items.cn: testis 加 -monium 构成 testimonium「证据、证词、证明」。

items.en: Anglo-French carried the noun into English law in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—法语在十三世纪把这个名词带入英格兰的法律用语。

items.en: From the first records testimony meant the statement of a witness, given in a case and open to challenge.
items.cn: 从最早的书证起，testimony 就指证人在案件中作出、可被质疑的陈述。

items.en: In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun widened to public declarations of faith and to any clear sign of a fact.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪，这个名词扩展到公开的信仰陈述以及任何明确的事实迹象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of testis is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is uncertain. The anatomical testis is a separate homonym and no derivation from the witness word is demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：testis 在拉丁语之前的历史属于重构，英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。解剖学意义上的 testis 是另一个同形词，尚无证据显示它由「证人」这个词派生。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same testis stock that are often confused; group two holds the kinds of statement a case may rest on.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 testis 词干、常被混淆的词；第二组是一桩案件可能依据的各类陈述。

entries.definition: From testari 'to make a will', built on testis: a document declaring one's wishes after death.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 testari「立遗嘱」，词根为 testis：声明身后意愿的文件。

entries.definition: A letter testifying to a person's character or service, rather than words spoken in court.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人品行或工作经历的信件，而不是庭上说的话。

entries.definition: A legal adjective for someone who has left a valid will, from the will-making sense of testari.
entries.definitionCN: 法律形容词，指留下有效遗嘱的人，取自 testari 的立遗嘱义。

entries.definition: An anatomical word from Latin testiculus; its relation to the witness word is not demonstrated.
entries.definitionCN: 解剖学术语，出自拉丁 testiculus；它与「证人」一词的关系未获证明。

entries.definition: The broad term for anything that proves a fact, of which testimony is one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指一切能证明事实的材料，证词只是其中一类。

entries.definition: A plain account of facts; it need not be sworn or given in court.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实的平实陈述，不必宣誓，也不必须在法庭作出。

entries.definition: A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation, usually for use in legal proceedings.
entries.definitionCN: 经宣誓或确认的书面陈述，通常用于法律程序。

entries.definition: Sworn testimony recorded out of court before trial, used later as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 审前在庭外录取的宣誓证词，供日后作为证据使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Testis 'witness' plus -monium: the words a witness brings.
normal.cn: testis「证人」加 -monium：证人带来的言辞。

normal.en: The family runs testify, testimony, testifier, testimonial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 testify、testimony、testifier 与 testimonial。

normal.en: Courts say give testimony and hear testimony; reporters say sworn testimony.
normal.cn: 法庭上说「提供证词」「听取证词」，报道里说「宣誓证词」。

normal.en: The abstract use is testimony to something: testimony to her patience.
normal.cn: 抽象用法是 testimony to：对她的耐心的明证。

normal.en: The anatomical testicle is a separate homonym, not a relative proved by derivation.
normal.cn: 解剖学上的 testicle 是另一个同形词，并非已证实的同族词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised over a book before the first sentence is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象在说出第一句之前，一只手先按在书上。

abstract.en: Picture a stone plaque that keeps saying what happened long after the witnesses have gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石牌，在证人都不在了之后仍不断说明发生过什么。

abstract.en: Picture a room where many separate voices are folded into one page.
abstract.cn: 想象许多彼此独立的声音被折进同一页纸里。

examples.en: The court heard testimony from six witnesses in two days.
examples.cn: 法庭在两天内听取了六名证人的证词。

examples.en: The broken tools are testimony to how little the crew had to work with.
examples.cn: 这些破损的工具说明施工队手里的条件多么有限。

examples.en: Her testimony to the commission was published with the exhibits.
examples.cn: 她向委员会所作的证词连同证物一并公布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「test（作证）+ imony」——站在证人席上说出所见：证词、见证

root: 拉丁 testimonium「证据、见证」= testis「证人」+ -monium；testis 更深来源不确定，与解剖学同形词无已证实的派生关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one witness in place while its voice moves: a sworn statement, an expert opinion, a public act of witnessing, a sign left by events, a written page, the combined voices of many, a declaration of faith and a statement to an inquiry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一位证人留在原处，只让他的声音移动：宣誓陈述、专家意见、公开见证、事件留下的明证、书面页、众人之声的合并、信仰陈述，以及向调查组的正式陈说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a witness at the stand with one hand raised, speaking sentence by sentence to a recorder.
core.cn: 核心意象：证人站在证人席上，一只手举起，一句一句地对速记员说话。

branches.en: THE SWORN VOICE: the same stand holds an eyewitness and a specialist explaining a field.
branches.cn: 宣誓的声音：同一个证人席上，既站着目击者，也站着解释专业的专家。

branches.en: BEYOND THE COURT: a life and a rebuilt square can both testify to something without speaking.
branches.cn: 走出法庭：一段人生与一座重建的广场都能不发一言地作证。

branches.en: ON PAPER: the statement is sworn in writing and read into the record.
branches.cn: 落在纸上：陈述以书面形式宣誓，再被读入案卷。

branches.en: MANY AT ONCE: separate statements are gathered into one body of testimony.
branches.cn: 多人同时：各自独立的陈述被汇成一份证词总体。

branches.en: ELSEWHERE SPEAKING: a congregation and a commission both ask for a formal personal account.
branches.cn: 在别处陈说：会众与调查委员会都要一份正式的个人陈述。

intro.en: Testimony is a Latin noun whose root, suffix and relatives all remain readable in English.
intro.cn: testimony 是一个拉丁名词，其词根、后缀与同族词在英语中仍然可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin testis 'witness' gives testimony, testify, testament and testimonial, all through the act of calling a witness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testis「证人」衍生 testimony、testify、testament 与 testimonial，都经由「传唤证人」这一动作。

items.example: The root names the person who speaks.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指出面说话的人。

items.example: The suffix turns the witness into the evidence produced.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「证人」转成由其产生的证据。

items.example: The testimony filled forty pages.
items.exampleCN: 证词写满了四十页。

items.example: Two neighbours testified.
items.exampleCN: 两位邻居作了证。

items.example: The testifier asked for protection.
items.exampleCN: 作证者要求保护。

items.example: The firm supplied a testimonial.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司出具了一封证明信。

items.example: The will was read as a testament.
items.exampleCN: 这份遗嘱被当作郑重声明宣读。

items.example: Two clerks attested the signature.
items.exampleCN: 两名职员证明了签名的真实性。

definition_zh: 作证；证实；（事物）表明、证明
definition_en: to give evidence in a court of law, or to show clearly that something is true
core_image: 手按誓词，把看到的那一幕原样说出来
scene: 法庭上，一名修理工把当天看到的火情按时间顺序讲给法官听。The mechanic must testify that the alarm had failed twice that month.
sceneCN: 这里 testify 指出庭给出证词（第 1 个义项：以证人身份在法庭上陈述）；句意为修理工作证说那个月警报器两次失灵。图中可辨识物件：证人席、工作服、警报器照片、法官的记录本。

pos.zh: 作证；提供证词
证实；表明；证明

derivatives.zh: 证明；证实（同出 testari 词根）

senses.title: Give evidence on the stand
senses.definition: to give evidence as a witness in a court
senses.definitionCN: 作为证人在法庭上提供证据
senses.example: The mechanic testified that the alarm had failed twice that month.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工作证说那个月警报器两次失灵。
senses.why: Testify is testis 'witness' plus -fy 'to make': the verb makes a person into a witness who speaks.
senses.whyCN: testify 是 testis「证人」加 -fy「使……成为」：这个动词把人变成开口的证人。

senses.title: State what one knows
senses.definition: to state in evidence what one saw, heard or knows
senses.definitionCN: 就所见、所闻或所知作出陈述
senses.example: Two neighbours testified that the lights were on all night.
senses.exampleCN: 两位邻居作证说整夜都亮着灯。
senses.why: The that-clause carries the content of the witness box into the record.
senses.whyCN: 这一从句结构把证人席上说出的内容带进案卷。

senses.title: Speak against someone
senses.definition: to give evidence that counts against an accused person
senses.definitionCN: 提供对被指控者不利的证据
senses.example: A former partner agreed to testify against the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 一名前合伙人同意作证指控这家公司。
senses.why: The preposition against turns the witness into an opposing party in the case.
senses.whyCN: 表示「反对」的介词把证人变成案件中的对立一方。

senses.title: Speak for someone
senses.definition: to give evidence in support of an accused person
senses.definitionCN: 提供对被指控者有利的证据
senses.example: His foreman testified for him at the sentencing hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 他的工头在量刑听证上为他作证。
senses.why: The same verb serves both sides; the preposition alone decides whose case is helped.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词对双方都适用，只由介词决定帮助哪一方。

senses.title: Things that bear witness
senses.definition: to show clearly that something is true, said of things rather than people
senses.definitionCN: 清楚表明某事为真，主语多为事物而非人
senses.example: The cracked foundations testify to years of subsidence.
senses.exampleCN: 开裂的地基证明多年下沉。
senses.why: Objects can testify in the same sense that a witness does: they make a fact evident to anyone who looks.
senses.whyCN: 物品「作证」与证人作证同理：它们让任何观看者都看清某项事实。

senses.title: Speak of faith in public
senses.titleCN: 宗教集会中公开讲述信仰
senses.definition: to give a personal account of religious experience to a group
senses.definitionCN: 在群体面前讲述个人的宗教经历
senses.example: She testified at the Wednesday meeting for the first time.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一次在周三聚会上讲述了自己的信仰经历。
senses.why: A congregation asks for the same formal personal account that a court asks of a witness.
senses.whyCN: 会众要求的，与法庭要求于证人的一样，都是正式的个人陈述。

senses.title: Address a hearing
senses.titleCN: 在听证会或委员会提供证言
senses.definition: to give formal evidence to a committee, commission or inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 向委员会、调查组或听证会提供正式证言
senses.example: The engineer testified before the transport committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这名工程师在交通委员会上作了证。
senses.why: The verb follows the witness wherever a formal record is being made.
senses.whyCN: 凡是要留下正式记录的地方，这个动词都跟着证人走。

senses.title: Establish by testimony
senses.definition: to establish or confirm something by giving evidence about it
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供相关证据来确立或确认某事
senses.example: The archivist testified to the authenticity of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 档案管理员作证确认这封信的真实性。
senses.why: The preposition to marks what the evidence is meant to establish, not merely what was seen.
senses.whyCN: 表示「指向」的介词标出证据所要确立的东西，而不只是看见的内容。

intro.en: Testify comes through Old French testifier from Latin testificari 'to bear witness', built on testis 'witness' and facere 'to make'. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: testify 经古法语 testifier 来自拉丁 testificari「作证」，由 testis「证人」与 facere「做、使」构成，十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Testis meant 'witness'; its deeper origin is not established, and the 'third person standing by' explanation is a reconstruction.
items.cn: testis 意为「证人」；其更深来源未获证明，「站在一旁的第三人」这一解释属于重构。

items.en: Testis plus facere produced testificari 'to bear witness, to call to witness'.
items.cn: testis 加 facere 构成 testificari「作证、传唤作证」。

items.en: Old French testifier carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 testifier 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: The earliest English use is legal: the verb describes a witness speaking in a case.
items.cn: 英语最早的用法属于法律：这个动词描述证人在案件中陈述。

items.en: By the sixteenth century objects and documents could testify as well, and the preposition to marked what they established.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，物品与文件也能「作证」，而表示「指向」的介词则标出它们所确立的内容。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of testis is a reconstruction, and the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：testis 在拉丁语之前的历史属于重构，最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same testari stock, including two built with different prefixes; group two holds verbs of swearing and affirming.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 testari 词干的词，其中两个由不同前缀构成；第二组是宣誓与确认类动词。

entries.definition: From testari in its will-making sense: a document that declares what happens after death.
entries.definitionCN: 取自 testari 的立遗嘱义：声明身后安排的文件。

entries.definition: A written statement praising a person's character or work, not evidence given in court.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞某人品行或工作表现的书面材料，不是庭上提供的证据。

entries.definition: Con- plus testari 'call to witness': to call witnesses together, hence to dispute or compete.
entries.definitionCN: con- 加 testari「传唤证人」：把证人一起叫来，因此指争辩或竞赛。

entries.definition: Pro- plus testari: to declare openly before witnesses, hence to object publicly.
entries.definitionCN: pro- 加 testari：在证人面前公开声明，因此指公开反对。

entries.definition: To confirm that something is true, often by signature or by evidence rather than by a court appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 确认某事为真，多凭签名或证据，而非出庭。

entries.definition: To make a solemn promise or statement under oath; it names the act of binding oneself to the truth.
entries.definitionCN: 在誓言下作出郑重承诺或陈述，强调的是让自己受真话约束的动作。

entries.definition: To give sworn evidence in a deposition, recorded before the trial rather than in open court.
entries.definitionCN: 在庭外录取的宣誓证词中作证，通常在审前进行。

entries.definition: To state formally that something is true, often as an alternative to swearing an oath.
entries.definitionCN: 正式声明某事为真，常用作宣誓的替代形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Testis 'witness' plus -fy 'make': to make someone a speaking witness.
normal.cn: testis「证人」加 -fy「使」：使人成为开口的证人。

normal.en: The family runs testify, testimony, testifier, testimonial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 testify、testimony、testifier 与 testimonial。

normal.en: Prepositions decide sides: testify against, testify for, testify to.
normal.cn: 介词决定立场：作证指控、为某人作证、证明某事。

normal.en: Objects testify too: the ruins testify to an older city.
normal.cn: 物品也会作证：废墟证明这里曾有更古老的城市。

normal.en: Contest and protest share the calling-of-witnesses root but add different prefixes.
normal.cn: contest 与 protest 共享「传唤证人」的词根，只是前缀不同。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised before the first word, not after it.
abstract.cn: 想象手在第一句话之前就已举起，而不是说完之后。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that keeps repeating what it saw, whether or not anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙不断重复它看见的事，无论有没有人问。

abstract.en: Picture two prepositions standing on either side of one witness.
abstract.cn: 想象两个介词站在同一位证人的两侧。

examples.en: Three former employees testified that the safety checks were skipped.
examples.cn: 三名前雇员作证说安全检查被跳过了。

examples.en: The empty shelves testify to how fast the town grew.
examples.cn: 空空的货架说明这座镇子发展得有多快。

examples.en: She was asked to testify to the date on the receipt.
examples.cn: 有人请她就收据上的日期作证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「test（作证）+ ify（使）」——使事实被说出来：作证、证实

root: 拉丁 testificari「作证」= testis（证人）+ facere（做、使）；testis 更深来源不确定。英语 testify 经古法语 testifier 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one witness through the building: into the stand, into a clause, onto one side of a case, then onto the other, out into objects, into a congregation, into a committee room and finally onto a point that the evidence is meant to settle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一位证人走遍整栋楼：走上证人席、进入从句、站到案件一方、再到另一方，随后走入物品、走进会众、走进委员会会议室，最后落在证据所要确立的那一点上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on the book, a voice giving an account in the order the events happened.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在书上，一个声音按事件发生的顺序把经过说出来。

branches.en: THE VOICE ON THE STAND: first the witness appears, then the content of the account is stated.
branches.cn: 证人席上的声音：先出现证人，再陈述叙述的内容。

branches.en: ONE SIDE: the same account is aimed at an accused person and counted against them.
branches.cn: 站在一方：同一段叙述被对准被指控者，成为对其不利的证据。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE: the account can equally be aimed in support, and only the preposition changes.
branches.cn: 站在另一方：同一段叙述也可以支持对方，变的只是介词。

branches.en: OBJECTS SPEAK: things make facts evident without any person taking the stand.
branches.cn: 物品开口：事物不需要任何人出庭，也能让事实变得清楚。

branches.en: OTHER ROOMS AND OTHER POINTS: a congregation, a committee and a fact to be established each borrow the courtroom verb.
branches.cn: 别的场合与别的落点：会众、委员会与待确立的事实都借用了这个法庭动词。

intro.en: Testify is a Latin verb whose root and second element still build English words.
intro.cn: testify 是一个拉丁动词，词根与第二个成分在英语中仍在构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin testis gives testimony, testament and testimonial; facere 'to make' gives -fy in testify and appears in many verbs of making.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testis 衍生 testimony、testament 与 testimonial；facere「做、使」在 testify 中化为 -fy，并出现在许多表示「使……成为」的动词里。

items.example: The root names the person who speaks.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指开口说话的人。

items.example: The second element turns the witness into an action.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分把「证人」变成一个动作。

items.meaning: to make; to cause to be
items.example: The suffix builds verbs such as testify and verify.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 testify、verify 一类动词。

items.example: The mechanic testified before the judge.
items.exampleCN: 修理工作证于法官面前。

items.example: The testimony was recorded verbatim.
items.exampleCN: 证词被逐字记录。

items.example: The testifier spoke for twenty minutes.
items.exampleCN: 作证者讲了二十分钟。

items.example: Two clerks attested the deed.
items.exampleCN: 两名职员为这份契据作证。

items.meaningCN: 把证人一起传唤，故指争辩、竞赛
items.example: The two sides contested the result.
items.exampleCN: 双方对结果提出争议。
