testari, testatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)
latinEntries.meaning: to witness, to make a will

definition_zh: 目击者；证人；证词；目睹；作证
definition_en: a person who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident, and can describe it
core_image: 路边的人停下脚步，把眼前发生的事记在心里，后来站上了证人席
scene: 十字路口发生碰撞，路边修车的人抬起头，把车牌和经过记了下来。The only witness saw the car leave the scene.
sceneCN: 这里 witness 指现场目击者（第 1 个义项：亲眼看到事件并可以描述的人）；句意为唯一的目击者看到那辆车离开了现场。图中可辨识物件：斑马线、碰撞的车辆、笔录本、路口信号灯。

pos.zh: 目击者；证人；证词
目睹；见证；作证；连署证明

senses.title: A person who saw it happen
senses.definition: someone who was present when an event happened and saw it themselves
senses.definitionCN: 事件发生时在场并亲眼看到的人
senses.example: The only witness saw the car leave the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 唯一的目击者看到那辆车离开了现场。
senses.why: Old English witnes joined wit 'knowledge' to an abstract noun suffix, so a witness is literally a person with knowledge of the event.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 witnes 由 wit「知识」加抽象名词后缀构成，因此证人字面上就是「对事件有知识的人」。

senses.title: A person who speaks in court
senses.definition: a person called to give evidence under oath in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中被传唤宣誓作证的人
senses.example: The witness answered each question in a low voice.
senses.exampleCN: 证人低声回答了每一个问题。
senses.why: The knowledge sense narrows in court to the person the court calls forward.
senses.whyCN: 「知情」义在法庭上收窄为被传唤上前的那个人。

senses.title: The evidence one gives
senses.definition: the testimony a person gives, especially in the fixed phrase bear witness
senses.definitionCN: 一个人提供的证词，尤见于「作证、见证」这一固定说法
senses.example: Her letters bear witness to a difficult decade.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书信见证了一段艰难的十年。
senses.why: A person and the words that person speaks are close enough that the same noun serves for both.
senses.whyCN: 人与他所说的话关系太近，以至于同一个名词可以兼指两者。

senses.title: The person who signs alongside
senses.definition: a person who watches a document being signed and signs it as proof
senses.definitionCN: 看着文件签署并签名加以证明的人
senses.example: The witness signed below the testator's name.
senses.exampleCN: 证人在立遗嘱人姓名下方签了名。
senses.why: Watching a signature is the same act as watching an event, applied to paper.
senses.whyCN: 看着别人签名与看着事件发生是同一个动作，只是落在纸上。

senses.title: To see an event happen
senses.definition: to see an event with one's own eyes
senses.definitionCN: 亲眼看到某个事件
senses.example: We witnessed the first snowfall of the year from the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在桥上看到了今年的第一场雪。
senses.why: The verb keeps the eye of the noun: to witness is simply to be the one who saw.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了名词里的那只眼睛：witness 就是那个看见的人。

senses.title: To live through a period
senses.definition: to be present during an important change or period
senses.definitionCN: 在重大变化或时期中在场并经历
senses.example: The town witnessed a doubling of its population in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇子在十年间见证了人口翻倍。
senses.why: A decade is treated like an event, and the town becomes the one who saw it.
senses.whyCN: 十年被当作一个事件，镇子则成了看见它的那个人。

senses.title: To sign as proof
senses.definition: to sign a document to confirm that a signature was made freely
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上签名，以确认签名出于自愿
senses.example: A clerk witnessed the deed and stamped the back.
senses.exampleCN: 一名职员为这份契据作证，并在背面盖了章。
senses.why: A signature is an event on paper, so watching it is the same act as watching anything else.
senses.whyCN: 签名是纸面上发生的一件事，看着它与其他「看着」是同一个动作。

senses.title: To show or attest
senses.definition: to show clearly that something is true, said of things and periods
senses.definitionCN: 清楚表明某事为真，主语多为事物或时期
senses.example: The empty shelves witness a supply that never arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的货架说明那批货始终没有到。
senses.why: Things can supply knowledge of a fact, which is all the noun ever required.
senses.whyCN: 物品也能提供关于事实的知识，而这正是这个名词一直要求的。

intro.en: Witness is a native English word: Old English witnes, built on wit 'knowledge, understanding' plus the abstract suffix -nes. It has no Latin source; Latin testis 'witness' is a semantic parallel, not a relative. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: witness 是英语本族词：古英语 witnes，由 wit「知识、理解」加抽象后缀 -nes 构成。它没有拉丁来源；拉丁 testis「证人」只是语义上的对应，并非同族词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wit meant 'mind, knowledge, understanding'; it survives in modern words such as witty and unwitting.
items.cn: wit 意为「心智、知识、理解」，仍存于 witty、unwitting 等现代词中。

items.en: -nes formed abstract nouns of state or quality, the ancestor of modern -ness.
items.cn: -nes 构成表示状态或性质的抽象名词，是现代 -ness 的前身。

items.en: Wit plus -nes gave witnes, 'knowledge of an event, a person who knows'.
items.cn: wit 加 -nes 构成 witnes，意为「对事件的知情、知情的人」。

items.en: From the fourteenth century the word is common in legal records for a person who attests facts or a signature.
items.cn: 从十四世纪起，这个词常出现在法律记录中，指证明事实或签名的人。

items.en: The verb appeared later, first meaning to attest a document and then to see an event.
items.cn: 动词用法出现较晚，先指为文件作证，后指亲眼看见事件。

items.en: The chain from Old English witnes is clear; the exact first use of the verb is not firmly dated, and the deeper pre-Germanic history of wit is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从古英语 witnes 下来的词源链清楚；动词用法的最早书证没有确切年代，而 wit 在日耳曼语之前的历史属于重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same wit stock and one compound; group two holds people who see events without necessarily speaking in court.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 wit 词干的词与一个复合词；第二组是看见事件、但不一定在法庭上开口的人。

entries.definition: The old noun for mind or quick understanding, and the source of witness.
entries.definitionCN: 这个古老名词意为心智或敏捷的理解力，也是 witness 的来源。

entries.definition: From wit plus -y: quick and amusing in speech, with no legal sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 由 wit 加 -y 构成：言辞机敏有趣，与法律无关。

entries.definition: A witness who saw the event personally, with the seeing organ spelt out in the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 亲眼看到事件的证人，复合词把「眼睛」直接写了出来。

entries.definition: Un- plus wit: not knowing that one is doing something, the opposite of informed awareness.
entries.definitionCN: un- 加 wit：并不知道自己在做什么，与「知情」相反。

entries.definition: A person who watches something, often deliberately and without any role in a case.
entries.definitionCN: 观看某事的人，往往是有意观察，且与案件无涉。

entries.definition: A person who is present by chance when something happens, with no duty to report it.
entries.definitionCN: 事件发生时恰好在场的人，没有报告的义务。

entries.definition: A person who watches an event from outside, stressing curiosity rather than knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 从旁观看事件的人，强调的是好奇而非知情。

entries.definition: A person who watches a planned public event such as a game or a ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 观看比赛、典礼等有组织的公开活动的人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Wit 'knowledge' plus the old noun suffix: a person who knows the event.
normal.cn: wit「知识」加古老的名词后缀：对事件知情的人。

normal.en: The family runs wit, witty, witness, eyewitness, unwitting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 wit、witty、witness、eyewitness 与 unwitting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the roles: key witness, bear witness, witness statement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：关键证人、作证、证人陈述。

normal.en: The verb keeps the same shape: witness an event, witness a signature.
normal.cn: 动词形式不变：目睹事件、为签名作证。

normal.en: Latin testis means the same thing but is not related; the resemblance is in meaning only.
normal.cn: 拉丁 testis 意思相同，却并无亲缘关系，相似只在语义上。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still while everyone else moves, because that person is watching.
abstract.cn: 想象所有人都走开，只有一个人站着不动，因为他在看。

abstract.en: Picture knowledge stored in a person rather than in a file.
abstract.cn: 想象知识存在一个人身上，而不是存在档案里。

abstract.en: Picture a second signature that exists only to say the first one was freely given.
abstract.cn: 想象第二个签名存在，只为说明第一个签名出于自愿。

examples.en: A neighbour who witnessed the fire described the smoke to the officer.
examples.cn: 一位目睹火灾的邻居向警官描述了烟的情况。

examples.en: The treaty witnessed a rare moment of agreement between the two states.
examples.cn: 这项条约见证了这两个国家罕见的一致时刻。

examples.en: No one was willing to bear witness against the foreman.
examples.cn: 没有人愿意出面作证指控那个工头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wit（知道）+ ness（状态）」——知道事情经过的人：目击者、证人

root: 古英语 witnes = wit（知识、心智）+ -nes（抽象名词后缀）；英语本族词，无拉丁同族，拉丁 testis 仅为语义对应。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same knowledge in view: the person who saw, the person the court calls, the words given, the second signature, the act of seeing, the act of living through, the act of signing and the way things themselves attest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着一份「知情」：看见的人、法庭传唤的人、说出的证词、第二个签名、看见的动作、经历的动作、签名作证的动作，以及事物本身的证明方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a passer-by stops at a crossing, burns the details into memory, and later takes the stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个路人在路口停下，把细节记进脑子里，后来走上证人席。

branches.en: THE PERSON WHO SAW: the original sense is simply the one who knows because he was there.
branches.cn: 看见的人：最原本的意思就是「因为当时在场而知情」的那个人。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE WORDS: the court calls the knower forward, and the noun also holds what he says.
branches.cn: 人与话：法庭把知情者叫到前面，而这个名词也装着他所说的内容。

branches.en: THE SECOND SIGNATURE: watching a pen move is watching an event on paper.
branches.cn: 第二个签名：看着笔移动，就是在纸面上看一件事发生。

branches.en: SEEING AND LIVING THROUGH: one may see a snowfall or live through a decade of change.
branches.cn: 看见与经历：可以看见一场雪，也可以经历十年的变迁。

branches.en: ATTEST AND ATTEST: a clerk signs, and an empty shelf speaks in the same direction.
branches.cn: 作证与作证：职员签下名字，空货架也朝同一个方向说明事实。

intro.en: Witness is a native English compound of an old noun and an old suffix; no Latin element enters it.
intro.cn: witness 是英语本族词，由一个古老名词与一个古老后缀构成，不含拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: the word belongs to the Germanic stock of English. Latin testis means 'witness' but is a parallel, not a relative, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁来源：这个词属于英语的日耳曼语层。拉丁 testis 虽意为「证人」，却只是语义对应而非同族，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The old noun still lives in modern English.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老名词仍活在现代英语里。

items.example: The suffix became modern -ness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀演变成现代的 -ness。

items.meaning: a person with knowledge of an event
items.example: The witness stood near the crossing.
items.exampleCN: 证人站在路口附近。

items.example: Two witnesses gave the same account.
items.exampleCN: 两名证人给出了相同的说法。

items.meaning: saw or attested in the past
items.example: She witnessed the collision.
items.exampleCN: 她目睹了那场碰撞。

items.example: The people witnessing the scene stayed back.
items.exampleCN: 围观的人留在后面。

items.meaning: one who saw with his own eyes
items.example: An eyewitness identified the van.
items.exampleCN: 一名目击者认出了那辆货车。

items.example: He was an unwitting carrier of the news.
items.exampleCN: 他无意中成了消息的传递者。

definition_zh: 证人陈述；证人证言书；目击者笔录
definition_en: a written account by a witness of what they saw, used as evidence in an investigation or a case
core_image: 一页签过名的陈述纸被夹进案卷，页脚是日期与警员编号
scene: 警员把目击者口述的内容逐条写下，请他在页脚签名。She signed her witness statement at the station.
sceneCN: 这里 witness statement 指证人签署的书面陈述（第 1 个义项：警方记录并用作证据的证人书面陈述）；句意为她在警局签了自己的证人陈述。图中可辨识物件：陈述纸、签名栏、警员编号、案卷夹。

pos.zh: 证人陈述（可数名词短语，复数 witness statements）
（英国程序）证人依规则交换的书面陈述

senses.title: A police-recorded statement
senses.titleCN: 警方记录的证人书面陈述
senses.definition: the written account a witness gives to the police, signed as accurate
senses.definitionCN: 证人向警方提供并签名确认内容属实的书面陈述
senses.example: She signed her witness statement at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在警局签了自己的证人陈述。
senses.why: The phrase joins the person who saw the event to the paper that records it, so the written record replaces the spoken voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把看见事件的人与记录其言的纸页连在一起，于是书面记录替代了口头陈述。

senses.title: An account given to investigators
senses.titleCN: 目击者向调查者提供的书面说明
senses.definition: a written description supplied to any official investigator
senses.definitionCN: 向任何官方调查者提交的书面描述
senses.example: Inspectors took a witness statement from every worker on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员向车间每位工人都取了一份证人陈述。
senses.why: Once the phrase leaves police stations it keeps the shape: a witness, a written account, a signature.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语离开警局后仍保持原形：一个证人、一份书面叙述、一个签名。

senses.title: A document tendered as proof
senses.titleCN: 作为证据提交的书面证词
senses.definition: a written statement put before a court or tribunal as evidence
senses.definitionCN: 提交给法院或审裁机构作为证据的书面陈述
senses.example: The bundle of witness statements ran to four hundred pages.
senses.exampleCN: 那捆证人陈述多达四百页。
senses.why: A bundle is the court's way of counting many separate pairs of eyes.
senses.whyCN: 一捆材料是法院清点许多双眼睛的方式。

senses.title: A record in an accident inquiry
senses.titleCN: 事故调查中的目击记录
senses.definition: the written account of a bystander collected after an accident
senses.definitionCN: 事故发生后采集的旁观者书面叙述
senses.example: The rail inquiry relied on witness statements taken the same night.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路调查依靠当晚采集的目击记录。
senses.why: An inquiry collects statements early, while memories are still close to the event.
senses.whyCN: 调查组尽早采集陈述，因为此时记忆还贴近事件。

senses.title: A step in civil procedure
senses.titleCN: 民事诉讼中交换的证人陈述
senses.definition: a signed statement exchanged between parties under court rules before trial
senses.definitionCN: 依法院规则在审前由各方交换的签名陈述
senses.example: Under the rules each side must exchange witness statements before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 依规则，双方必须在听证前交换证人陈述。
senses.why: Civil procedure gave the compound a fixed place in the timetable, not merely a record of what someone saw.
senses.whyCN: 民事程序给这个复合词确定了时间表上的位置，它不再只是「某人看见了什么」的记录。

senses.title: A form in insurance claims
senses.titleCN: 保险理赔中的目击者说明
senses.definition: a written account from a bystander attached to a claim file
senses.definitionCN: 附在理赔档案中的旁观者书面说明
senses.example: The insurer asked for a witness statement from the driver behind her.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司要求她后方那辆车的司机提供目击者说明。
senses.why: An insurer needs the same structure as a court: a named person, a signed account, a date.
senses.whyCN: 保险公司需要与法院相同的结构：一个具名的人、一份签名的叙述、一个日期。

senses.title: A quotation in reporting
senses.titleCN: 媒体引述的目击者说法
senses.definition: the account a reporter attributes to a person who was present
senses.definitionCN: 记者归到在场者名下的叙述
senses.example: The report quoted a witness statement describing the smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 报道引用了一段描述烟情的目击者说法。
senses.why: Journalism borrows the legal label to make a quotation look attested.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业借用这个法律标签，让引语看起来经过核实。

senses.title: A spoken account written down
senses.definition: a loose term for an account written down from a witness's dictation
senses.definitionCN: 对「按证人口述记录下来的说法」的宽泛称呼
senses.example: The clerk typed the witness statement while the man spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 那名男子说话时，职员把他的陈述打了下来。
senses.why: When a clerk writes down dictation, the paper records a voice rather than a signed account.
senses.whyCN: 当职员照口述记录时，纸页记录的是声音，而不是一份签名的陈述。

intro.en: Witness statement is an English compound of two elements: witness, a native word from Old English witnes, and statement, from state plus -ment, where state goes back to Latin status 'standing, position'. The compound is recorded in police and legal usage from the nineteenth century onward. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: witness statement 是由两个成分构成的英语复合词：witness 是古英语 witnes 的本族词，statement 由 state 加 -ment 构成，而 state 可追溯至拉丁 status「站立、状态」。这个复合词自十九世纪起见于警务与法律用法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Witnes joined wit 'knowledge' to an abstract suffix and named a person who knows an event.
items.cn: witnes 由 wit「知识」加抽象后缀构成，指对事件知情的人。

items.en: Status meant 'standing, position, condition' and gives English state and status.
items.cn: status 意为「站立、位置、状况」，衍生英语 state 与 status。

items.en: State plus -ment produced statement, first a statement of facts and later a formal account.
items.cn: state 加 -ment 构成 statement，最初指事实陈述，后指正式叙述。

items.en: Witness statement appears in police practice once statements were written down and signed as routine procedure.
items.cn: 当书面陈述与签名成为例行程序后，witness statement 便出现在警务实践中。

items.en: Modern civil rules gave the phrase a precise slot: a signed document exchanged before trial.
items.cn: 现代民事规则给这个短语一个精确位置：审前交换的签名文件。

items.en: Both parts of the compound are well documented and the chain is clear; only the earliest use of the exact phrase is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：复合词的两个成分都有充分记录，构词链清楚，只有这个确切短语的最早书证没有确定年代。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical compounds that differ by one element; group two holds the legal documents most often confused with a witness statement.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个成分的近形复合词；第二组是最常与证人陈述混淆的法律文件。

entries.definition: Any formal account of facts; without witness it does not say who gave it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何正式的事实陈述；不带 witness 就不说明是谁说的。

entries.definition: Re- plus statement: a second version of an account, often in clearer words.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀 re-（表示「再、重新」）加 statement：同一说法的第二次表述，往往更清楚。

entries.definition: Under- plus statement: an account that deliberately makes something sound smaller than it is.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀 under-（表示「不足」）加 statement：故意把某事说得比实际更轻的表述。

entries.definition: Mis- plus statement: a statement containing an error, whether careless or deliberate.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀 mis-（表示「错误」）加 statement：含有错误的陈述，无论疏忽还是有意。

entries.definition: A written statement confirmed by oath before an authorised person; the oath is what defines it.
entries.definitionCN: 在有权者面前宣誓确认的书面陈述，定义性特征是誓言。

entries.definition: Sworn testimony recorded out of court during litigation, used later at trial.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼过程中在庭外录取的宣誓证词，供审判时使用。

entries.definition: The evidence a witness gives orally, not the paper it is written on.
entries.definitionCN: 证人口头提供的证据，而不是承载它的纸页。

entries.definition: A formal statement on paper, which may or may not carry an oath.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的书面陈述，可能宣誓也可能没有。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Witness plus statement: the person who saw, plus the paper that records it.
normal.cn: witness 加 statement：看见的人，加上记录其言的纸。

normal.en: The compound keeps a regular plural: witness statements.
normal.cn: 这个复合词的复数是规则的：witness statements。

normal.en: Procedure verbs pair with it: make, sign, exchange, retract.
normal.cn: 程序动词与它搭配：作出、签署、交换、撤回。

normal.en: Police and civil courts both use it, but with different routines around it.
normal.cn: 警方与民事法院都用它，只是围绕它的程序不同。

normal.en: Affidavit and deposition are sworn documents; a witness statement need not be sworn in the same way.
normal.cn: affidavit 与 deposition 都是宣誓文件，证人陈述则未必以同样方式宣誓。

abstract.en: Picture a spoken sentence pressed flat onto paper and given a signature.
abstract.cn: 想象一句口头的话被压平到纸上，再配上一个签名。

abstract.en: Picture a case file where each page is one person's pair of eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一册案卷，每一页都是一个人的一双眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a statement that has been signed but not yet tested.
abstract.cn: 想象一份已经签名、尚未经受检验的陈述。

examples.en: The officer read the witness statement back to her before she signed.
examples.cn: 警员在她签名前把证人陈述读了一遍给她听。

examples.en: Both parties must exchange witness statements two weeks before the hearing.
examples.cn: 双方必须在听证前两周交换证人陈述。

examples.en: A single witness statement cannot carry the whole case.
examples.cn: 仅凭一份证人陈述撑不起整个案子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「witness（证人）+ statement（陈述）」——证人签字的书面陈述

root: 英语复合词：witness（古英语 witnes，本族词）+ statement（state + -ment，state 出自拉丁 status「站立、状况」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one sheet of paper: it starts in a police station, then serves any investigator, then a court bundle, an accident file, a civil timetable, an insurance claim, a news quotation and finally a loose name for dictation written down.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一页纸走：先在警局，再供任何调查者使用，随后进入庭审材料、事故档案、民事时间表、理赔档案、新闻引述，最后成为「按口述记录」的宽泛说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed sheet of paper with a date and an officer number at the foot, clipped into a case file.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页签过名的陈述纸，页脚写着日期与警员编号，被夹进案卷。

branches.en: THE FIRST SETTING: a police station statement and the same practice used by any investigator.
branches.cn: 最初的场景：警局里的陈述，以及任何调查者采用的同样做法。

branches.en: ON THE RECORD: a bundle for court and a file for an accident inquiry both hold signed pages.
branches.cn: 进入记录：庭审材料与事故档案里装的都是签名页。

branches.en: THE TIMETABLE: civil rules turn the sheet into a step to be completed before trial.
branches.cn: 时间表：民事规则把这页纸变成审前必须完成的一步。

branches.en: ELSEWHERE USED: an insurer's file and a newspaper quotation both borrow the phrase.
branches.cn: 别处借用：保险档案与报纸引述都借用了这个说法。

branches.en: THE LOOSE NAME: dictation typed down by a clerk is still called by the same phrase.
branches.cn: 宽泛的称呼：职员照口述打下来的记录，仍用同一个说法。

intro.en: Witness statement is an English compound: one native element and one element that goes back to Latin status.
intro.cn: witness statement 是英语复合词：一个本族成分，一个可追溯至拉丁 status 的成分。

latinIntro.en: Only statement has a Latin line, through state and status. Witness is Germanic, so the Latin list records status and its relatives rather than any supposed source of the whole phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 statement 有拉丁线索，经 state 上溯至 status。witness 属日耳曼语层，因此拉丁词条记录 status 及其同族，而不是整个短语的所谓来源。

items.meaning: a person who knows an event
items.example: The witness signed at the foot.
items.exampleCN: 证人在页脚签了名。

items.example: The state of the file was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 档案的状态被记录在案。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of stating into a thing stated.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「陈述」的动作变成「陈述」的成品。

items.example: The statement ran to three pages.
items.exampleCN: 这份陈述有三页长。

items.meaning: a signed account by a witness
items.example: The officer took a witness statement.
items.exampleCN: 警员取了一份证人陈述。

items.example: The statements were exchanged on time.
items.exampleCN: 这些陈述按时交换了。

items.example: She was ready to testify.
items.exampleCN: 她准备好作证了。

items.example: The testimony matched the sheet.
items.exampleCN: 证词与那份书面材料一致。

definition_zh: 审判；试验；考验；选拔赛；试用
definition_en: a formal examination of evidence in a court to decide whether someone is guilty
core_image: 法庭上双方把材料依次摆开，法官听完两边再作判断
scene: 法庭里，双方把各自材料依次呈上，法官在笔记上记下要点。The trial resumed after a two-week recess.
sceneCN: 这里 trial 指法庭审判（第 1 个义项：法院对案件进行的正式审理）；句意为庭审在两周休庭后恢复。图中可辨识物件：法官席、证据箱、速记本、旁听席。

pos.zh: 审判；试验；考验；选拔赛；试用
试用；试行（英式拼写 trialled）

derivatives.zh: 试训运动员；试验参与者

senses.title: A court hearing of a case
senses.definition: a formal hearing in which a court examines evidence and decides a case
senses.definitionCN: 法院审查证据并裁决案件的正式审理
senses.example: The trial resumed after a two-week recess.
senses.exampleCN: 庭审在两周休庭后恢复。
senses.why: Trial and try come from Old French trier 'to sift, pick out'; a court tries a case by sifting the evidence.
senses.whyCN: trial 与 try 出自古法语 trier「筛、挑」；法院审案正是把证据筛一遍。

senses.title: A test of a product or method
senses.definition: an act of testing whether something works well
senses.definitionCN: 检验某物是否可用的过程
senses.example: The first trial of the new pump failed in cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 新泵的第一次试验在冷水中失败。
senses.why: The sifting sense broadened from legal judgment to any careful testing.
senses.whyCN: 「筛选」义从法律判断扩展到任何仔细的检验。

senses.title: A hard experience
senses.definition: a difficult experience that tests a person's patience or strength
senses.definitionCN: 考验人的耐心或意志的艰难经历
senses.example: Caring for three patients at once was a trial of her patience.
senses.exampleCN: 同时照顾三名病人是对她耐心的考验。
senses.why: Patience is put through a test, and the word for a legal test of facts serves for a test of character.
senses.whyCN: 耐心被送进一场检验，而那个用于检验事实的词，也用来检验品性。

senses.title: A sporting qualifying event
senses.definition: an event in which competitors are tested for a place on a team
senses.definitionCN: 为争取队伍名额而进行的测试比赛
senses.example: He won the final trial and was named to the squad.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢了最后一场选拔赛，入选了队伍。
senses.why: Selection by testing is the sifting sense applied to people rather than evidence.
senses.whyCN: 以测试选拔，就是把「筛选」用在人身上而不是证据上。

senses.title: A test plot in farming
senses.definition: a small planting used to test a seed or a treatment before wider use
senses.definitionCN: 在大面积推广前检验种子或处理方式的小块种植
senses.example: The rice trial produced two tonnes more per hectare.
senses.exampleCN: 这块水稻试验田每公顷多产了两吨。
senses.why: A small plot is a test because the harvest is judged before the seed is trusted on a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 小块地之所以是试验，因为要先评判收成，才敢把种子用到整片田里。

senses.title: A medical study
senses.definition: a controlled study testing a treatment in patients
senses.definitionCN: 在病人身上检验某种治疗的对照研究
senses.example: The drug entered a phase three trial last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药去年春天进入三期临床试验。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the testing sense and fixed it in the phrase clinical trial.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「检验」义，并把它固定在「临床试验」这一说法里。

senses.title: A probationary period
senses.definition: a period during which something is used provisionally before a decision
senses.definitionCN: 在作出决定前临时使用的一段时间
senses.example: The clerk was hired on a three-month trial.
senses.exampleCN: 这名职员以三个月试用期受聘。
senses.why: Time itself becomes the test: the thing is used for a while and then judged.
senses.whyCN: 时间本身成了检验：先用一段时间，再作判断。

senses.title: To test something in use
senses.definition: to use something for a period in order to judge it
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内使用某物以便评判
senses.example: The city will trial the new bus route for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 该市将试行这条新公交线路六个月。
senses.why: The noun turned back into a verb, keeping the same sifting idea.
senses.whyCN: 名词又转回动词，保留同一个「筛一筛」的意思。

intro.en: Trial comes from Anglo-Norman and Old French trial, from the verb trier 'to sift, pick out', whose own origin is unknown; the deeper source is not Latin. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trial 来自盎格鲁—诺曼语与古法语 trial，出自动词 trier「筛选、挑出」，而 trier 本身的来源不明，更深来源并非拉丁语。十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trier meant 'to sift, to pick out', used of grain, cloth and disputed facts.
items.cn: trier 意为「筛、挑出」，可用于谷物、布料与有争议的事实。

items.en: The noun trial named the act of sifting, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 trial 指「筛选」这一动作，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: By the fifteenth century trial meant the sifting of evidence in a court, the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，trial 已指法庭上对证据的筛选，这一义项如今占主导。

items.en: The same word served for testing metals, medicines and machines, where sifting is literal.
items.cn: 同一个词也用于检验金属、药物与机器，那里的「筛」是字面意义上的。

items.en: From the nineteenth century trial named a contest that selects players or animals.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，trial 指选拔运动员或动物的比赛。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of Old French trier is unknown, and no Latin source can be shown; the exact first English citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：古法语 trier 的来源不明，无法证明有拉丁来源；英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes with entirely different roots; group two holds the hearings and tests that trial is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近而词根完全不同的词；第二组是常与 trial 混淆的审理与检验。

entries.definition: From a verb meaning to draw behind; it names a track or a path, with no testing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 出自意为「拖在后面」的动词，指痕迹或小径，与「检验」无关。

entries.definition: From trivium, the three elementary subjects, hence commonplace and unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 trivium「三科基础课」，因此指平常、不重要。

entries.definition: From tribunus, a Roman official; it names a judging body, not a test.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 tribunus「罗马官员」，指审判机构，而非试验。

entries.definition: From tributum 'something assigned', from tribuere 'to allot': a payment or a mark of respect.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 tributum「分配之物」，源头是 tribuere「分配」：指贡赋或敬意。

entries.tag: a session, not a full trial
entries.definition: A session where a court or committee listens to argument, often before the main decision.
entries.definitionCN: 法院或委员会听取意见的一次会议，常在主要决定之前。

entries.definition: Any procedure for checking quality or performance, legal or otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 检验质量或性能的任何程序，法律内外皆可。

entries.definition: A procedure designed to discover something new rather than to judge a finished thing.
entries.definitionCN: 为发现新知识而设计的程序，不是为评判已有之物。

entries.definition: Any formal step in a legal action, of which a trial is the final hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 法律行动中的任何正式步骤，审判是其中最后的审理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old French trier 'sift': a trial sifts evidence, seeds or players.
normal.cn: 古法语 trier「筛」：审判筛证据，试验筛种子，选拔赛筛选手。

normal.en: The family runs try, trial, trials, trialist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 try、trial、trials 与 trialist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: stand trial, clinical trial, trial run, field trial.
normal.cn: 固定搭配切分义项：受审、临床试验、试运行、田间试验。

normal.en: Saying something is on trial covers both a defendant and a new machine.
normal.cn: 说某物 on trial，既可以是被告受审，也可以是新机器在试用。

normal.en: Trail and tribunal look close but come from drawing behind and from a Roman official.
normal.cn: trail 与 tribunal 外形相近，却分别出自「拖在后面」与罗马官员。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve held over a pile: what stays on top decides the answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子举在料堆上方：留在上面的那部分决定答案。

abstract.en: Picture a key turned in a lock several times before the door is trusted.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在锁里转了好几次，门才被信任。

abstract.en: Picture a season of practice matches played only to choose a team.
abstract.cn: 想象一整个赛季的练习赛，只是为了挑出一支队伍。

examples.en: The trial was moved to a larger courtroom because of public interest.
examples.cn: 由于公众关注，审判被移到更大的法庭。

examples.en: Researchers ran a trial of the vaccine on four hundred volunteers.
examples.cn: 研究人员在四百名志愿者身上试验了这种疫苗。

examples.en: The long walk home was a trial for the children.
examples.cn: 那段长途步行回家路对孩子们是一场考验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tri（筛）+ al」——把证据、种子、选手都筛一遍：审判、试验、选拔

root: 古法语 trier「筛选、挑出」+ 名词后缀 -al；trier 的更深来源不明，并非拉丁来源。英语 trial 经盎格鲁—诺曼语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one sieve working: a court sifts evidence, industry sifts a design, life sifts patience, sport sifts players, farms sift seed, medicine sifts a drug, an employer sifts a new hire, and the verb sifts in use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一只筛子继续工作：法院筛证据，工业筛设计，生活筛耐心，体育筛选手，农田筛种子，医学筛药物，雇主筛新人，动词则在「使用中」筛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve held over a pile, with what remains on top deciding the judgment.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只筛子举在料堆上方，留在上面的东西决定判断结果。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM SIEVE: evidence is sifted in public and a verdict follows.
branches.cn: 法庭之筛：证据当众被筛一遍，随后作出裁决。

branches.en: SIEVE AND STRAIN: a pump or a patience can both be put through the same wringer.
branches.cn: 筛与熬：水泵与耐心都能过同一道关口。

branches.en: CHOOSING FROM MANY: players and seed varieties are both selected by testing.
branches.cn: 从多中选：选手与种子品种都靠测试被挑选出来。

branches.en: TIME AS THE TEST: a drug is followed for months, a new clerk for three.
branches.cn: 以时间检验：药物要跟踪数月，新职员要试用三个月。

branches.en: THE VERB RETURNS: the sieve becomes an action again when a city trials a route.
branches.cn: 动词回归：当城市试行一条线路时，筛子又变回一个动作。

intro.en: Trial is an English noun from Old French, with no established Latin source for its root.
intro.cn: trial 是来自古法语的英语名词，其词根没有可证的拉丁来源。

latinIntro.en: The root trier 'to sift' has an unknown origin, so there is no Latin relative to record; the Latin list stays empty and only native suffixes build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 trier「筛」来源不明，因此没有可记录的拉丁同族词；拉丁词条留空，词族只靠本族后缀构成。

items.meaning: the act of sifting or testing
items.example: The trial began at nine.
items.exampleCN: 审判九点开始。

items.example: The trials ran for two years.
items.exampleCN: 这些试验持续了两年。

items.example: They tried the new route.
items.exampleCN: 他们试了那条新线路。

items.example: The method was tried in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这个方法在冬天试用过。

items.example: It was a trying week.
items.exampleCN: 那是考验人的一周。

items.meaning: a person taking part in a trial
items.example: The trialist played forty minutes.
items.exampleCN: 试训球员打了四十分钟。

items.meaning: a first performance used as a test
items.example: The trial run found two faults.
items.exampleCN: 试运行发现了两处故障。

items.meaning: a test carried out in real conditions
items.example: The field trial lasted one season.
items.exampleCN: 实地试验持续了一个季节。

definition_zh: 罪犯；犯罪的；刑事的；（口语）可耻的、极糟的
definition_en: a person who has committed a crime; relating to crime or its punishment
core_image: 被告席上的人低着头，身后的记录本列着一串案由
scene: 法庭后门，一名刚被判刑的人被带下台阶，记者在门外等着拍照。The criminal was escorted out through a side door.
sceneCN: 这里 criminal 指被判有罪的人（第 1 个义项：犯了罪的人）；句意为这名罪犯从侧门被带了出去。图中可辨识物件：侧门、押解人员、记者相机、台阶。

pos.zh: 罪犯；刑事被告
犯罪的；刑事的；（口语）可耻的、极糟的

senses.title: A person who broke the law
senses.definition: a person who has committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 实施了犯罪行为的人
senses.example: The criminal was escorted out through a side door.
senses.exampleCN: 这名罪犯从侧门被带了出去。
senses.why: Criminal is crimen 'charge, crime' plus -al, first an adjective 'of crime' and then a noun for the person charged.
senses.whyCN: criminal 是 crimen「指控、罪行」加 -al，先作「与罪有关的」形容词，再转为指被控之人的名词。

senses.title: Belonging to criminal law
senses.definition: relating to the branch of law that deals with offences and penalties
senses.definitionCN: 与处理罪行与刑罚的法律分支有关
senses.example: The case moved from civil to criminal court.
senses.exampleCN: 案件从民事法院转到刑事法院。
senses.why: The adjective sorts the case into the branch of law that punishes, and the branch name follows.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把案件归入负责惩处的那一支法律，随后就有了这一分支的名称。

senses.title: Amounting to an offence
senses.titleCN: 构成犯罪的、应受刑罚的
senses.definition: serious enough in law to be punished as an offence
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上严重到可作为罪行受罚
senses.example: Destroying the files was a criminal act, not a clerical slip.
senses.exampleCN: 销毁档案是犯罪行为，不是文书失误。
senses.why: The adjective moves from naming a branch of law to judging a single act serious enough for that branch.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从命名法律分支，转为判断单个行为严重到足以进入该分支。

senses.title: The person in the dock
senses.definition: the accused person standing trial, seen from the court's point of view
senses.definitionCN: 受审的被指控者，从法庭视角称呼
senses.example: The criminal stood while the verdict was read.
senses.exampleCN: 宣读裁决时，被告站着。
senses.why: Used as a noun, the adjective lets a court name the person in the dock without repeating the charge.
senses.whyCN: 形容词作名词，让法庭能称呼被告席上的人而不必重复罪名。

senses.title: Papers and records
senses.definition: used in fixed phrases about records, checks and history
senses.definitionCN: 用于记录、审查与履历一类固定说法
senses.example: A criminal record can block a job application for years.
senses.exampleCN: 犯罪记录可以在多年内妨碍求职。
senses.why: Records are the paper trail of the law, so the adjective attaches to the file rather than to the person.
senses.whyCN: 记录是法律留下的纸面痕迹，因此形容词附着在档案上而不是人身上。

senses.title: Colloquial: beyond excuse
senses.titleCN: 口语：极其糟糕、不可原谅的
senses.definition: in informal use, shamefully bad or wasteful
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指糟糕或浪费得不可原谅
senses.example: It is criminal to throw away food in a district like this.
senses.exampleCN: 在这样的城区扔掉食物简直不可原谅。
senses.why: The word for a legal offence became a word for anything that ought to be punished, even a wasted meal.
senses.whyCN: 表示法律罪行的词，转用来指任何「该受罚」的事，哪怕只是一顿被浪费的饭。

senses.title: A habitual offender
senses.definition: a person who commits offences repeatedly, often as a way of life
senses.definitionCN: 反复实施犯罪、常以此为生的人
senses.example: The file described him as a career criminal.
senses.exampleCN: 档案把他描述为职业罪犯。
senses.why: A career is a pattern, and the word extends from one act to a way of life repeated over years.
senses.whyCN: 「职业」是一种模式，这个词于是从一次行为扩展到多年重复的生活方式。

senses.title: A label for the system
senses.titleCN: 刑事司法领域的限定用法
senses.definition: used to name the institutions that catch, try and punish offenders
senses.definitionCN: 用于命名侦查、审理与惩处罪犯的整套机构
senses.example: She works in criminal justice research.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事刑事司法研究。
senses.why: Naming the institutions is the last step: the adjective stops describing people and starts describing a system.
senses.whyCN: 命名机构是最后一步：形容词不再描述人，而开始描述一套体系。

intro.en: Criminal comes through Middle French criminel from Latin criminalis, built on crimen 'charge, accusation, crime'. It is recorded in English from the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: criminal 经中古法语 criminel 来自拉丁 criminalis，词根为 crimen「指控、控告、罪行」，十五世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crimen meant 'charge, indictment, accusation' before it meant the deed itself.
items.cn: crimen 先指「指控、起诉、控告」，之后才指罪行本身。

items.en: Crimen plus -alis produced criminalis 'of a charge, of an offence'.
items.cn: crimen 加 -alis 构成 criminalis「与指控、罪行有关的」。

items.en: Middle French criminel carried both the adjective and the noun into English.
items.cn: 中古法语 criminel 把形容词与名词一并带入英语。

items.en: English kept criminal for offences against the state and civil for disputes between private parties.
items.cn: 英语用 criminal 指危害国家的罪行，用 civil 指私人之间的纠纷。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the adjective was applied to anything shameful, such as a criminal waste.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个形容词被用到任何可耻的事上，如「不可原谅的浪费」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link of crimen to cernere 'to sift' is generally thought but not proved, and no older root is certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：一般认为 crimen 与 cernere「筛」有关，但未获证实，更古老的词根也无法确定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the crimen stock plus one look-alike; group two holds the names for people who offend.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 crimen 词干的词，外加一个形近词；第二组是对犯罪者的各种称呼。

entries.definition: The offence itself; criminal is the adjective and the person, crime is the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指罪行本身；criminal 是形容词或指人，crime 指行为。

entries.definition: Crimen plus Greek -logia: the academic study of crime and offenders.
entries.definitionCN: crimen 加希腊 -logia：研究犯罪与罪犯的学科。

entries.definition: To make someone appear guilty, literally to put a charge onto a person.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人显得有罪，字面是「把指控放进某人身上」。

entries.definition: From discriminare, built on discernere 'to separate': to tell things apart, not to charge anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 discriminare，词根是 discernere「分辨」：区分事物，与指控无关。

entries.definition: A person who commits an offence, used in official and legal prose without moral colour.
entries.definitionCN: 实施违法行为的人，官方与法律文书用语，不带道德色彩。

entries.definition: A person found guilty by a court, stressing the verdict rather than the act.
entries.definitionCN: 被法院判定有罪的人，强调裁决而非行为。

entries.definition: A person convicted of a serious crime, chiefly in American legal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 被判重罪的人，主要用于美国法律语境。

entries.definition: The person responsible for a wrong, often used of small troubles and informal blame.
entries.definitionCN: 对过错负责的人，常用于小事与口语归责。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Crimen 'charge' plus -al: of a charge, then the person charged.
normal.cn: crimen「指控」加 -al：先指「与指控有关的」，再指被控的人。

normal.en: The family runs crime, criminal, criminality, criminalize, criminology, incriminate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 crime、criminal、criminality、criminalize、criminology 与 incriminate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the law: criminal law, criminal record, criminal justice.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律领域：刑法、犯罪记录、刑事司法。

normal.en: Courts pair it with civil: criminal court, civil court.
normal.cn: 法庭上常与 civil 对照：刑事法院、民事法院。

normal.en: Discriminate looks like the family but comes from separating, not from charging.
normal.cn: discriminate 看似同族，却来自「分辨」而非「指控」。

abstract.en: Picture a folder with a charge written on the cover before any deed is described.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹，封面先写着指控，里面的行为还没描述。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked side exit, kept for people the court has finished with.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着侧门的门，专供法院已经处理完的人走。

abstract.en: Picture a word that leaves the courtroom and starts judging a wasted meal.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词走出法庭，开始评判一顿被浪费的饭。

examples.en: The criminal had already served two sentences for the same offence.
examples.cn: 这名罪犯已因同一罪行服过两次刑。

examples.en: Criminal law treats the act differently from a breach of contract.
examples.cn: 刑法对这类行为的处理与违约不同。

examples.en: Leaving the evidence unread for a year was a criminal oversight.
examples.cn: 把证据搁了一年没人看，是极不可原谅的疏忽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「crime（罪）+ inal」——与罪有关的、犯了罪的人

root: 拉丁 criminalis = crimen（指控、罪行）+ -alis；crimen 与 cernere「筛」的联系一般认为存在但未证实。英语经中古法语 criminel 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a person to a branch of law to a quality of acts, then to a courtroom seat, a paper record, an informal rebuke, a way of life and a whole system of institutions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个人走向一个法律分支，再到行为的性质、法庭上的座位、纸面记录、口语责备、一种生活方式，最后是一整套机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure at the dock with a record book open behind, a list of charges running down the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：被告席上的人低着头，身后摊开的记录本上列着一串案由。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the noun names the one who committed the deed.
branches.cn: 那个人：名词指实施了该行为的人。

branches.en: THE LAW AND THE ACT: the adjective marks the branch of law and the seriousness of what was done.
branches.cn: 法律与行为：形容词既标出法律分支，也标出行为的严重程度。

branches.en: INSIDE THE SYSTEM: the accused has a seat, and the system keeps a file on him.
branches.cn: 体系之内：被告有一个座位，体系也为他保留一份档案。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE COURT: the same word scolds a wasted meal as if it deserved punishment.
branches.cn: 法庭之外：同一个词会责备一顿被浪费的饭，仿佛它该受罚。

branches.en: A LIFE AND A SYSTEM: a career offender and a field of justice research both carry the label.
branches.cn: 一种人生与一套体系：职业罪犯与刑事司法研究都带着这个标签。

intro.en: Criminal is a Latin adjective and noun whose root still builds a large English family.
intro.cn: criminal 是一个拉丁形容词兼名词，其词根在英语中仍构成一大族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin crimen gives crime, criminal, criminality, criminology and incriminate; -alis supplies the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crimen 衍生 crime、criminal、criminality、criminology 与 incriminate；-alis 提供形容词词尾。

items.example: The root starts as a charge, not as a deed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根最初指指控，而不是行为本身。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.meaning: of crime; a person who offends
items.example: The criminal left by the side door.
items.exampleCN: 罪犯从侧门离开。

items.example: The crime was reported at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 案件在黎明时报了案。

items.meaning: the quality or extent of crime
items.example: The study measured criminality by district.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究按街区衡量犯罪状况。

items.example: The state criminalized the sale.
items.exampleCN: 该州把这种销售定为犯罪。

items.example: Criminology grew out of prison reform.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪学由监狱改革中发展而来。

items.example: The note incriminated two clerks.
items.exampleCN: 这份记录使两名职员显得有罪。

definition_zh: 罪行；犯罪；犯罪活动；（口语）憾事、不该做的事
definition_en: an illegal act that can be punished by law
core_image: 夜里被撬开的窗，窗台上留着半枚鞋印，警笛在街角响起
scene: 清晨的店铺门口，玻璃碎了一地，店主蹲下查看被撬开的锁。Police recorded the theft as a serious crime.
sceneCN: 这里 crime 指依法应受处罚的违法行为（第 1 个义项：可受刑罚的违法行为）；句意为警方把这起盗窃记为严重罪行。图中可辨识物件：碎玻璃、被撬的锁、警戒带、记录板。

pos.zh: 罪行；犯罪行为（可数）
犯罪活动；犯罪现象（不可数）

senses.title: One punishable offence
senses.titleCN: 一项可受刑罚的违法行为
senses.definition: a single act that the law forbids and punishes
senses.definitionCN: 法律禁止并加以处罚的单个行为
senses.example: Police recorded the theft as a serious crime.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把这起盗窃记为严重罪行。
senses.why: Latin crimen began as 'charge, accusation': a crime is first what can be laid against someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 crimen 最初意为「指控、控告」：罪行首先是可以拿来指控某人的事。

senses.title: Crime as a phenomenon
senses.definition: the general activity of breaking the law, treated as a mass
senses.definitionCN: 把违法活动当作一个整体现象看待
senses.example: The link between poverty and crime is disputed.
senses.exampleCN: 贫穷与犯罪之间的关联仍有争议。
senses.why: Once acts are counted together, the plural becomes an uncountable field, like weather.
senses.whyCN: 当许多行为被合在一起计数，复数就变成一整片不可数的领域，像天气一样。

senses.title: A class of offences
senses.definition: a category of offence defined by its target or its gravity
senses.definitionCN: 按侵害对象或严重程度划分的一类违法行为
senses.example: Crimes against cultural property carry separate penalties.
senses.exampleCN: 侵害文化财产的罪行另有刑罚。
senses.why: Categories are made by the object a deed damages, so the same noun takes a preposition and a plural.
senses.whyCN: 类别按行为损害的对象划分，因此同一个名词可以带介词、用复数。

senses.title: Sin and guilt
senses.definition: a moral wrong for which one is answerable, whether or not a court is involved
senses.definitionCN: 无论是否经法院处理、个人须为其负责的道德过错
senses.example: In the old sermons, envy was a crime of the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的布道里，嫉妒是心里的罪。
senses.why: Before law took the word over, crimen already named a charge that could be brought on moral grounds.
senses.whyCN: 在法律接管这个词之前，crimen 就已指可依道德理由提起的责难。

senses.title: Colloquial: a great pity
senses.definition: something shameful or wasteful, said with exaggeration
senses.definitionCN: 以夸张口气说某事可耻或浪费
senses.example: It is a crime to let that orchard go to weeds.
senses.exampleCN: 让那片果园荒成杂草，真是件憾事。
senses.why: The legal word survives as hyperbole: whatever ought not to happen is called a crime against good sense.
senses.whyCN: 法律词在夸张中存活下来：任何不该发生的事都被说成对常理的犯罪。

senses.title: A reported case
senses.definition: an incident recorded by the police as an offence
senses.definitionCN: 被警方作为违法事件记录下来的具体案情
senses.example: The detective was assigned the crime the same morning.
senses.exampleCN: 刑警当天上午就接手了这起案件。
senses.why: Police paperwork turns an act into a case with a number, and the word shifts from deed to file.
senses.whyCN: 警方的文书把行为变成有编号的案件，这个词于是从「行为」转向「案卷」。

senses.title: Organised criminal activity
senses.definition: the operations of groups that make money through illegal means
senses.definitionCN: 以非法手段牟利的团伙活动
senses.example: Organised crime moved the goods through three ports.
senses.exampleCN: 有组织犯罪把货物转经三个港口。
senses.why: A group can commit many crimes as one operation, so the mass use serves for an enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 一个团伙可以把许多罪行当作一项经营，因此不可数用法也能指一门「生意」。

senses.title: Crime in statistics
senses.titleCN: 犯罪统计与犯罪率语境
senses.definition: the measured level of offending in a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某时期被测得的违法水平
senses.example: Reported crime fell while unreported crime rose.
senses.exampleCN: 报案数下降，未报案的犯罪却上升了。
senses.why: Policy talk turns acts into numbers, and the word becomes a rate on a chart.
senses.whyCN: 政策话语把行为变成数字，这个词于是成了图表上的一条比率线。

intro.en: Crime comes through Old French crime from Latin crimen 'charge, accusation, crime', a third-declension noun with the stem crimin-. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: crime 经古法语 crime 来自拉丁 crimen「指控、控告、罪行」，是词干为 crimin- 的第三变格法名词，十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crimen first meant a charge or an accusation; only later did it name the deed charged.
items.cn: crimen 最初指指控或控告，后来才指被指控的行为。

items.en: The oblique stem crimin- is why English has criminal, criminality and criminology rather than crimen-based forms.
items.cn: 斜格词干 crimin- 正是英语出现 criminal、criminality、criminology 而非直接取自 crimen 的词形的原因。

items.en: Old French crime carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, already meaning the offence.
items.cn: 古法语 crime 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，当时已指罪行。

items.en: English law sorted offences into crimes, misdemeanours and lesser breaches, and crime became the general term.
items.cn: 英国法把违法行为分为重罪、轻罪与更轻的违规，crime 逐渐成为总称。

items.en: From the nineteenth century crime was counted, mapped and debated as a social quantity.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，crime 被计数、绘图并作为社会数量加以讨论。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link of crimen to cernere 'to sift' is generally thought but not demonstrated; the exact first English citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：一般认为 crimen 与 cernere「筛」有关，但未获证实；英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds the legal family and one look-alike; group two holds words for offences ranked by formality.
note.cn: 第一组是同一法律词族与一个形近词；第二组是各类违法行为的称呼，按正式程度排列。

entries.definition: The adjective of crime and the person who commits one; crime is the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: crime 的形容词形式，也指犯罪的人；crime 指行为本身。

entries.definition: The academic field that measures and explains crime.
entries.definitionCN: 测量并解释犯罪现象的学科。

entries.definition: To place a charge on someone, hence to make them look guilty.
entries.definitionCN: 把指控放到某人身上，因此指使其显得有罪。

entries.definition: From discernere 'to separate': to distinguish, with no connection to crimen.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 discernere「分辨」：区分事物，与 crimen 无关。

entries.definition: The general legal term for a breach of the law, common in statutes and police reports.
entries.definitionCN: 违法行为的通用法律术语，常见于法条与警方通报。

entries.definition: A serious crime carrying heavier penalties, chiefly in American law.
entries.definitionCN: 可处较重刑罚的严重罪行，主要用于美国法。

entries.definition: Bad behaviour in general, which may never reach a court.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指不良行为，未必进入司法程序。

entries.definition: A breaking of a rule, a right or a boundary, often civil rather than criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则、权利或边界，常属民事而非刑事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Crimen 'charge' first, the deed second: a crime is what can be charged.
normal.cn: crimen 先指「指控」，后指行为：罪行就是可以被指控的事。

normal.en: The stem crimin- builds criminal, criminality, criminology, incriminate.
normal.cn: 词干 crimin- 构成 criminal、criminality、criminology、incriminate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: crime rate, crime scene, organized crime.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：犯罪率、犯罪现场、有组织犯罪。

normal.en: Countable for acts, uncountable for the phenomenon: a crime, but also crime in general.
normal.cn: 数单个行为时用可数，谈整体现象时用不可数。

normal.en: Discriminate is a false friend from separating, not from charging.
normal.cn: discriminate 是假朋友，来自「分辨」而非「指控」。

abstract.en: Picture a window forced open while the street is asleep.
abstract.cn: 想象街道沉睡时，一扇窗被撬开。

abstract.en: Picture a charge written on a form before the deed is described in words.
abstract.cn: 想象表格上先写了指控，行为还没用文字描述。

abstract.en: Picture a number on a chart that stands for thousands of separate nights.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的一个数字，背后是成千上万个不同的夜晚。

examples.en: Theft from a parked car is treated as a minor crime in most cities.
examples.cn: 在多数城市，从停放车辆上偷东西被视为轻微罪行。

examples.en: Crime fell in the district after the lighting was improved.
examples.cn: 照明改善后，这个区的犯罪率下降了。

examples.en: She called it a crime to cut down a tree that old.
examples.cn: 她说砍掉那么老的树真是件憾事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「crime（罪）」——被法律禁止并可处罚的行为：罪行

root: 拉丁 crimen（词干 crimin-）「指控、控告、罪行」；crimen 与 cernere「筛」的联系一般认为存在但未证实。英语经古法语 crime 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a single punishable act to a social mass, then to categories, to moral guilt, to exaggeration, to a police file, to organised operations and to a rate on a chart.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单个可罚行为走向社会总量，再到各类罪行、道德罪责、夸张说法、警方案卷、团伙活动，最后成为图表上的比率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window forced open at night, half a footprint on the sill, a siren turning the corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里被撬开的窗，窗台上留着半枚鞋印，警笛在街角响起。

branches.en: THE SINGLE ACT: one deed that the law forbids and punishes.
branches.cn: 单个行为：法律禁止并处罚的一项行为。

branches.en: THE MASS AND THE CLASSES: all such acts together, or one category sorted by target.
branches.cn: 总量与类别：把所有这类行为合起来看，或按侵害对象分出一类。

branches.en: THE INNER CHARGE: guilt that needs no courtroom, inherited from the older sense of accusation.
branches.cn: 内心的指控：不需要法庭的罪责，承自更早的「控告」义。

branches.en: PITY AND FILE: the same word scolds a wasted orchard and labels a case at the station.
branches.cn: 憾事与案卷：同一个词既责备荒废的果园，也在警局给案件贴上标签。

branches.en: SCALE AND NUMBER: organised operations and a falling rate are the same acts seen from far away.
branches.cn: 规模与数字：团伙活动与下降的比率，都是从远处看同一批行为。

intro.en: Crime is a Latin noun whose oblique stem still builds most of the English family.
intro.cn: crime 是一个拉丁名词，其斜格词干至今构成英语词族的大部分。

latinIntro.en: Latin crimen, stem crimin-, gives crime, criminal, criminality, criminology and incriminate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crimen 的词干 crimin- 衍生 crime、criminal、criminality、criminology 与 incriminate。

items.example: The noun starts life as a charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指一项指控。

items.meaningCN: 用于接词尾的斜格词干
items.example: Most English relatives are built on this stem.
items.exampleCN: 英语中多数同族词都建立在这个词干上。

items.example: The crime was reported at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 案件在黎明时报了案。

items.example: The file listed three crimes.
items.exampleCN: 案卷列了三项罪行。

items.meaning: of crime; a person who offends
items.example: The criminal left by the side door.
items.exampleCN: 罪犯从侧门离开。

items.meaning: the quality or extent of crime
items.example: Criminality varies by district.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪状况因街区而异。

items.example: Parliament criminalized the trade.
items.exampleCN: 议会把这种交易定为犯罪。

items.example: Criminology began with prison records.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪学始于监狱记录。
