definition_zh: 犯罪性；犯罪倾向；犯罪状况（不可数）
definition_en: the quality or state of being criminal, or the extent of crime in a place or a group
core_image: 一张城市地图上，几个街区被红笔圈出，旁边写着案件数量
scene: 研究者在社区中心展示一张标满红点的地图，说明不同街区的案件分布。Researchers measured criminality by district rather than by city.
sceneCN: 这里 criminality 指某地的犯罪状况（第 1 个义项：犯罪的性质与程度）；句意为研究者按街区而非整座城市衡量犯罪状况。图中可辨识物件：地图、红点、统计表、投影幕。

pos.zh: 犯罪性；犯罪倾向（不可数）
犯罪状况；犯罪程度（社会学用语）

senses.title: The quality of being criminal
senses.titleCN: 犯罪的性质与程度（总称）
senses.definition: the quality or degree of being criminal, considered in the abstract
senses.definitionCN: 抽象地看待「属于犯罪」这一性质及其程度
senses.example: Researchers measured criminality by district rather than by city.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者按街区而非整座城市衡量犯罪状况。
senses.why: Criminal plus -ity makes a quality noun, the abstract counterpart of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: criminal 加 -ity 构成性质名词，是形容词的抽象对应形式。

senses.title: Crime levels in a place
senses.titleCN: 某地或某时期的犯罪状况
senses.definition: the level of offending recorded in a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某时期记录到的违法水平
senses.example: Criminality in the port rose after the patrols were cut.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻削减后，港区的犯罪状况恶化。
senses.why: Sociology turned the quality into a measurable state of a place.
senses.whyCN: 社会学把这一性质变成某地可测量的状态。

senses.title: Legal quality of an act
senses.titleCN: 行为在法律上构成犯罪的属性
senses.definition: the character that makes an act punishable under criminal law
senses.definitionCN: 使某项行为在刑法下可受处罚的性质
senses.example: The court examined the criminality of the conduct, not its motive.
senses.exampleCN: 法院审查的是该行为是否构成犯罪，而不是其动机。
senses.why: In law the word names an attribute of conduct, which is why it appears in judgments about whether a charge can be brought.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上这个词指行为的属性，因此常见于判断能否提起指控的判决中。

senses.title: Organised criminality
senses.definition: the scale of coordinated illegal activity in a region or an industry
senses.definitionCN: 某地区或某行业中协同违法活动的规模
senses.example: Criminality in the freight business was organised around two families.
senses.exampleCN: 货运业的犯罪活动围绕两个家族组织起来。
senses.why: Coordination gives crime a size and a structure, and the quality noun measures that structure.
senses.whyCN: 协同让犯罪有了规模与结构，这个性质名词衡量的正是那种结构。

senses.title: The object of criminology
senses.definition: the subject matter that criminology measures, explains and compares
senses.definitionCN: 犯罪学所测量、解释与比较的对象
senses.example: The journal treats criminality as a social process rather than a trait.
senses.exampleCN: 这份期刊把犯罪现象当作社会过程，而不是个人特质。
senses.why: A discipline needs a name for what it measures, and the abstract noun supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科需要为它所测量的东西命名，这个抽象名词正好提供。

senses.title: A tendency in a person
senses.definition: an individual disposition toward committing offences
senses.definitionCN: 个人实施违法行为的倾向
senses.example: Early writers linked criminality to the shape of the skull.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作者把犯罪倾向与颅骨形状联系起来。
senses.why: Psychology and early criminology used the noun for a trait inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 心理学与早期犯罪学用这个名词指人身上的某种特质。

senses.title: Crime at the level of a state
senses.titleCN: 国家或制度层面的犯罪行为
senses.definition: offending carried out or tolerated by state institutions
senses.definitionCN: 由国家机构实施或纵容的违法行为
senses.example: Scholars of state criminality study deportation and detention records.
senses.exampleCN: 研究国家犯罪的学者考察驱逐与拘留记录。
senses.why: If institutions can act like offenders, the same quality noun can be predicated of a state.
senses.whyCN: 如果机构能像犯罪者一样行动，同一个性质名词就可以用来陈述国家。

senses.title: Contrast with civil wrongs
senses.titleCN: 与民事不法相对的刑事性质
senses.definition: the criminal character that distinguishes an act from a civil wrong
senses.definitionCN: 区分刑事行为与民事侵权的性质
senses.example: The criminality of the act did not remove the victim's right to sue.
senses.exampleCN: 该行为构成犯罪，并不取消受害人起诉的权利。
senses.why: The boundary with civil wrongs is a boundary of character, so the noun names the character itself.
senses.whyCN: 与民事不法的界线是性质的界线，因此这个名词命名的正是那种性质。

intro.en: Criminality is an English formation from criminal plus the noun suffix -ity, which goes back to Latin -itas. Criminal itself comes from Latin criminalis, from crimen 'charge, accusation'. The noun is recorded from the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: criminality 是在英语内部由 criminal 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，-ity 可上溯至拉丁 -itas。criminal 本身来自拉丁 criminalis，词根为 crimen「指控、控告」。这个名词十七世纪起有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crimen named a charge before it named the deed, and its stem crimin- underlies the family.
items.cn: crimen 先指指控，后指行为，其词干 crimin- 支撑整个词族。

items.en: Criminalis meant 'of a charge, of an offence', and English criminal came from it.
items.cn: criminalis 意为「与指控、罪行有关的」，英语 criminal 由此而来。

items.en: -itas formed abstract quality nouns, the ancestor of English -ity.
items.cn: -itas 构成抽象性质名词，是英语 -ity 的前身。

items.en: English writers built criminality to name the state of being criminal, first in moral and legal argument.
items.cn: 英语作者构造 criminality 来指「属于犯罪的状态」，最初用于道德与法律论辩。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the noun became a technical measure of offending in a population.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个名词成为衡量人群违法状况的技术指标。

items.en: The formation criminal plus -ity is transparent and the chain is clear; only the earliest English citation is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：criminal 加 -ity 的构成一目了然，词源链清楚，只有英语最早书证没有确定年代。

note.en: Group one holds the crimen family and one look-alike; group two holds terms for the measured side of crime.
note.cn: 第一组是 crimen 词族与一个形近词；第二组是犯罪「可测量一面」的相关术语。

entries.definition: The adjective and the person; criminality is the abstract quality, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指形容词或犯罪的人；criminality 是抽象性质，不指人。

entries.definition: The discipline that studies criminality; the two words are often used as if interchangeable but are not.
entries.definitionCN: 研究犯罪性的学科；两者常被当作可互换，其实不同。

entries.definition: To put a charge on someone, not to describe the level of crime.
entries.definitionCN: 把指控加到某人身上，而不是描述犯罪水平。

entries.definition: From discernere 'to separate': to distinguish, unrelated to crimen.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 discernere「分辨」：区分事物，与 crimen 无关。

entries.definition: Offending by young people, from Latin delinquere 'to fail'; narrower in age than criminality.
entries.definitionCN: 青少年的违法行为，出自拉丁 delinquere「失职」；在年龄范围上比 criminality 更窄。

entries.definition: Behaviour that departs from social norms, only some of which is criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离社会规范的行为，其中只有一部分构成犯罪。

entries.definition: A condition in which law is not enforced, wider than the rate of offences.
entries.definitionCN: 法律得不到执行的状况，比犯罪率更宽泛。

entries.definition: Bad conduct in general, with no statistical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指不良行为，完全不含统计意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Criminal plus -ity: the state of being criminal, treated as a quantity.
normal.cn: criminal 加 -ity：把「属于犯罪」的状态当作一个量来看。

normal.en: The family runs crime, criminal, criminality, criminalize, criminology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 crime、criminal、criminality、criminalize 与 criminology。

normal.en: Sociology pairs it with rates and causes: rates of criminality, root causes of criminality.
normal.cn: 社会学常与比率和成因搭配：犯罪率、犯罪根源。

normal.en: The word is uncountable: one speaks of criminality, not of a criminality.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数：说 criminality，而不说 a criminality。

normal.en: Criminology studies criminality; the two words are related but not synonyms.
normal.cn: 犯罪学研究 criminality；两者相关，但不是同义词。

abstract.en: Picture a map with certain blocks shaded darker than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，某些街区被涂得比别处更暗。

abstract.en: Picture a quality that can be poured into a chart and read as a curve.
abstract.cn: 想象一种性质被倒进图表，读出来是一条曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a word that turns a person's act into a property of a whole district.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词把个人的行为变成整个街区的属性。

examples.en: Comparative criminality is hard to measure when reporting habits differ.
examples.cn: 当各地的报案习惯不同时，犯罪状况很难比较衡量。

examples.en: The report traced juvenile criminality to school exclusion.
examples.cn: 报告把青少年犯罪追溯到被学校排除这一原因。

examples.en: They argued that the criminality of the act depends on the wording of the statute.
examples.cn: 他们主张该行为是否构成犯罪取决于法条的措辞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「criminal（犯罪的）+ ity（性质）」——犯罪的性质与程度

root: 英语 criminal（拉丁 criminalis，词根 crimen「指控、罪行」）+ 名词后缀 -ity（拉丁 -itas，表性质）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from an abstract quality to a measured place, then to a legal attribute, an organised scale, a research object, a personal tendency, a state practice and a contrast with civil wrongs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从抽象性质走向可测量的地区，再到法律属性、有组织规模、研究对象、个人倾向、国家行为，以及与民事不法的对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a city map with certain blocks ringed in red and case numbers written beside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张城市地图，几个街区被红笔圈出，旁边写着案件数量。

branches.en: THE QUALITY AND ITS AMOUNT: first an abstract property, then a level recorded in a place.
branches.cn: 性质与数量：先是抽象属性，再是某地记录到的水平。

branches.en: THE LEGAL TEST: the word names what makes conduct punishable, regardless of motive.
branches.cn: 法律判断：这个名词指使行为可受刑罚的性质，与动机无关。

branches.en: SCALE AND STUDY: coordinated activity has a size, and a discipline takes that size as its object.
branches.cn: 规模与研究：协同活动有大小，而一门学科把这一大小当作研究对象。

branches.en: INSIDE A PERSON: psychology reads the noun as a disposition or trait.
branches.cn: 一个人之内：心理学把这个名词读成倾向或特质。

branches.en: THE STATE AND THE CIVIL LINE: institutions can offend, and the criminal character marks a boundary against civil wrongs.
branches.cn: 国家与民事界线：机构也会违法，而刑事性质划出了与民事侵权的界线。

intro.en: Criminality joins a Latin-derived adjective to a Latin-derived suffix inside English.
intro.cn: criminality 在英语内部把一个拉丁来源的形容词与一个拉丁来源的后缀接在一起。

latinIntro.en: Crimen gives criminal and its relatives; -itas supplies the abstract ending that becomes -ity.
latinIntro.cn: crimen 衍生 criminal 及其同族词；-itas 提供抽象词尾，后演变为 -ity。

items.example: The stem carries the legal idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载法律含义。

items.example: The criminal court sat on Monday.
items.exampleCN: 刑事法院周一开庭。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a quality noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成性质名词。

items.meaning: the state or extent of crime
items.example: Criminality was mapped by ward.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪状况按选区绘制成图。

items.example: The criminal was released in spring.
items.exampleCN: 这名罪犯在春天获释。

items.meaning: in a criminal way; to a criminal degree
items.example: The files were criminally neglected.
items.exampleCN: 这些档案被严重疏忽，几近犯罪。

items.example: The law criminalized the practice.
items.exampleCN: 法律把这种做法定为犯罪。

items.example: Criminology measures what courts record.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪学测量法院记录下来的东西。

definition_zh: 把……定为犯罪；使入罪；（被动）使被当作罪犯对待
definition_en: to make an activity illegal and punishable by law
core_image: 议事厅里举起的手通过一条新条文，原本寻常的动作从此被写进罪名
scene: 议会大厅里，电子屏上的票数跳过半数，旁听席有人低声议论。Lawmakers voted to criminalize the sale of unlicensed medicine.
sceneCN: 这里 criminalize 指通过立法把某行为定为犯罪（第 1 个义项：以法律把行为入罪）；句意为立法者投票把无证销售药品定为犯罪。图中可辨识物件：议事厅、电子计票屏、法案文本、旁听席。

pos.zh: 把……定为犯罪；使入罪
使某人或某群体被当作罪犯对待

senses.title: Make an act an offence
senses.titleCN: 立法把某行为定为犯罪
senses.definition: to place an activity under criminal law so that it can be punished
senses.definitionCN: 把某项活动纳入刑法范围，使其可受处罚
senses.example: Lawmakers voted to criminalize the sale of unlicensed medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 立法者投票把无证销售药品定为犯罪。
senses.why: Criminalize is criminal plus -ize 'to make': the verb makes a deed into a crime.
senses.whyCN: criminalize 是 criminal 加 -ize「使……成为」：这个动词把行为变成罪行。

senses.title: Turn lawful conduct unlawful
senses.titleCN: 使原本合法的事变为违法
senses.definition: to change the legal status of conduct that was previously permitted
senses.definitionCN: 改变原本被允许行为的法律地位
senses.example: The new rules criminalized what had been a routine practice for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 新规把几十年来的例行做法变成了违法行为。
senses.why: Making something criminal is the reverse of permitting it, and the suffix carries that reversal.
senses.whyCN: 把某事物定为犯罪，就是「允许」的反面，而这个词尾正承担这一翻转。

senses.title: Reach a category of people
senses.titleCN: 把某类人纳入刑事处罚范围
senses.definition: to bring a group of people within the reach of criminal penalties
senses.definitionCN: 使某一群体落入刑事处罚的适用范围
senses.example: Advocates argued that the measure criminalized the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 反对者主张这项措施把穷人推入刑事处罚范围。
senses.why: A law aimed at an act catches the people who habitually perform it, so the verb extends to them.
senses.whyCN: 针对行为的法律会网住在习惯性从事该行为的人，因此这个动词也扩展到人身上。

senses.title: Name an international crime
senses.titleCN: 在国际法层面定为罪行
senses.definition: to classify conduct as a crime under international law
senses.definitionCN: 依国际法把某行为归为罪行
senses.example: The statute criminalized the recruitment of child soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 该规约把征募儿童兵定为罪行。
senses.why: International tribunals apply the same verb to conduct that no single state can punish alone.
senses.whyCN: 国际法庭把同一个动词用于任何单个国家都无法独自惩处的行为。

senses.title: Treat as criminal in practice
senses.titleCN: 执法实践中事实上按犯罪处理
senses.definition: to treat conduct as criminal through enforcement even where the law is unclear
senses.definitionCN: 在法律不明晰时通过执法事实上按犯罪处理
senses.example: Critics said the police had criminalized homelessness by sweeping the camps.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说警方清理营地，事实上把无家可归者当作罪犯。
senses.why: Enforcement can do what a statute has not done, which is why the verb is used for de facto criminalization.
senses.whyCN: 执法可以做到法条尚未做到的事，因此这个动词也用于「事实上的入罪化」。

senses.title: Attach a penalty
senses.titleCN: 使某行为承受刑罚后果
senses.definition: to subject conduct to a penalty, fine or imprisonment
senses.definitionCN: 使某行为承受罚金、刑罚或监禁的后果
senses.example: The amendment criminalized late payment with a heavy fine.
senses.exampleCN: 修正案以重罚把逾期付款定为犯罪。
senses.why: A penalty is what makes a new offence real, so the verb is also used for the sanction itself.
senses.whyCN: 刑罚才让新罪名落到实处，因此这个动词也用于制裁本身。

senses.title: Make it an offence locally
senses.titleCN: 地方或行业规章层面的入罪化
senses.definition: to create an offence at the level of a local ordinance or a professional code
senses.definitionCN: 在市镇条例或行业规范层面新设罪名
senses.example: The city council criminalized camping in the station forecourt.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会把在车站前庭露营定为犯罪。
senses.why: Local bodies can create offences too, so the verb descends from statutes to ordinances.
senses.whyCN: 地方机构也能设罪名，因此这个动词从法条下降到条例。

senses.title: Be treated as a criminal
senses.titleCN: 被动用法：被当作罪犯对待
senses.definition: to be dealt with as a criminal, whether or not a charge follows
senses.definitionCN: 被按罪犯对待，无论随后是否提起指控
senses.example: Patients were criminalized for seeking help too often.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因求助过于频繁而被当作罪犯看待。
senses.why: The passive lets the verb describe an experience rather than a legislative act.
senses.whyCN: 被动式让这个动词可以描述一种经历，而不只是立法动作。

intro.en: Criminalize is an English verb from criminal plus the suffix -ize, which reaches English through French from Late Latin -izare and Greek -izein 'to make, to do'. It is recorded from the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: criminalize 是英语动词，由 criminal 加后缀 -ize 构成；-ize 经法语来自晚期拉丁 -izare，再上溯希腊 -izein「使、做」。这个词十九世纪起有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crimen 'charge, accusation' supplies the first part of criminal and hence of the verb.
items.cn: crimen「指控、控告」提供 criminal 的前半部分，也提供这个动词的前半部分。

items.en: Criminal named both the adjective and the person before the verb existed.
items.cn: 在动词出现之前，criminal 已兼指形容词与犯罪的人。

items.en: Greek -izein meant 'to make, to do'; Late Latin -izare and French -iser carried it into English as -ize.
items.cn: 希腊 -izein 意为「使、做」；晚期拉丁 -izare 与法语 -iser 把它带入英语，成为 -ize。

items.en: The verb appeared in legal and reforming writing, naming the act of putting conduct under criminal law.
items.cn: 这个动词出现在法律与改革写作中，指把行为纳入刑法的动作。

items.en: In the twentieth century it spread to debates about policing, morality and international tribunals.
items.cn: 二十世纪，它扩展到关于警务、道德与国际法庭的争论。

items.en: The chain criminal plus -ize is clear and the suffix has a documented history; only the earliest citation of the verb is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：criminal 加 -ize 的词源链清楚，后缀的历史也有记录，只有这个动词的最早书证没有确定年代。

note.en: Group one holds the crimen family, including the verb's direct relatives; group two holds verbs that restrain conduct by other means.
note.cn: 第一组是 crimen 词族，含这个动词的直接同族词；第二组是以其他手段限制行为的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective and the person; the verb differs by making something into an offence.
entries.definitionCN: 指形容词与犯罪的人；动词则多了「使某行为成为罪行」的意思。

entries.definition: The abstract state of being criminal, not the act of creating an offence.
entries.definitionCN: 指「属于犯罪」的抽象状态，而不是设置罪名的动作。

entries.definition: The academic study of crime, with no legislative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 研究犯罪的学科，不含立法含义。

entries.definition: De- 'away from' plus criminalize: to remove an offence from criminal law.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 criminalize：把某项罪名从刑法中移除。

entries.definition: To declare something illegal, often by decree; it stresses the ban more than the penalty.
entries.definitionCN: 宣布某事物非法，多带命令色彩，强调禁止甚于刑罚。

entries.definition: To forbid something officially; a ban may be administrative rather than criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁止某事，可能是行政禁令而非刑事罪名。

entries.definition: To forbid by law or rule, with no necessary link to prosecution.
entries.definitionCN: 依法或依规禁止，与是否起诉没有必然联系。

entries.definition: To impose a disadvantage or fine for conduct, which may stop short of a criminal charge.
entries.definitionCN: 对某行为施加不利后果或罚款，未必构成刑事指控。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Criminal plus -ize 'to make': making a deed into a crime.
normal.cn: criminal 加 -ize「使」：把行为做成罪行。

normal.en: The family runs criminal, criminality, criminalize, criminalization, decriminalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 criminal、criminality、criminalize、criminalization 与 decriminalize。

normal.en: Legislative verbs pair with it: vote to criminalize, move to criminalize.
normal.cn: 立法动词与它搭配：投票入罪、提议入罪。

normal.en: Its opposite is decriminalize, and the pair marks the two directions of a statute.
normal.cn: 它的反义动词是 decriminalize，这一对词标出法条的两种方向。

normal.en: The passive is common when the subject is a group of people rather than an act.
normal.cn: 当主语是一群人而不是某行为时，被动式更常见。

abstract.en: Picture a line being drawn on the ground where none was before.
abstract.cn: 想象在地上画出一条以前不存在的线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall, changing what counts as ordinary.
abstract.cn: 想象礼堂里举起一只手，改变了什么算寻常。

abstract.en: Picture a door that used to be open being quietly closed and locked.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇原本敞开的门被悄悄关上并上锁。

examples.en: The statute criminalized the possession of unregistered weapons.
examples.cn: 该法规把持有未登记武器定为犯罪。

examples.en: Several cities have moved to criminalize sleeping in public spaces.
examples.cn: 若干城市已着手把在公共场所睡觉入罪。

examples.en: The tribunal criminalized the recruitment of children under fifteen.
examples.cn: 该法庭把征募十五岁以下儿童定为罪行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「criminal（罪犯）+ ize（使）」——使某事变成犯罪：入罪化

root: 英语 criminal（拉丁 criminalis，词根 crimen）+ 动词后缀 -ize（晚期拉丁 -izare，出自希腊 -izein「使、做」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one legislative act outward: a statute names an offence, changes a permitted practice, reaches a group, enters international law, is applied in the street, carries a penalty, appears in local rules and finally lands on the person treated as a criminal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次立法动作向外扩散：法条设定罪名、改变原本允许的做法、触及一个群体、进入国际法、在街头被执行、附带刑罚、出现在地方规则里，最后落到被当作罪犯的那个人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands raised in a chamber, a new clause on the screen, and an ordinary act turning into a charge.
core.cn: 核心意象：议事厅里举起的手，屏幕上一条新条文，一个寻常动作变成一项罪名。

branches.en: THE STATUTE: an activity is named and its legal status is reversed.
branches.cn: 法条：某项活动被点名，其法律地位被翻转。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE REACHED: penalties extend to a class of people, not only to a deed.
branches.cn: 被触及的人：刑罚延伸到一类人身上，而不只针对行为。

branches.en: ABOVE AND BELOW: international law names the crime, while patrols apply it in the street.
branches.cn: 上与下：国际法设定罪名，巡逻在街头执行。

branches.en: THE PENALTY AND THE PARISH: a fine attaches to the act, and a local ordinance creates the offence.
branches.cn: 刑罚与地方：罚金附着在行为上，地方条例也能新设罪名。

branches.en: THE PERSON AT THE END: the passive turns the verb into an experience of being treated as a criminal.
branches.cn: 最后落到人：被动式把这个动词变成「被当作罪犯」的经历。

intro.en: Criminalize is an English verb: a Latin-derived base plus a Greek-derived verb suffix.
intro.cn: criminalize 是英语动词：一个拉丁来源的词基，加一个希腊来源的动词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Crimen gives criminal; -izare, the Late Latin form of Greek -izein, gives the verb ending -ize and also builds organize, modernize and legalize.
latinIntro.cn: crimen 提供 criminal；希腊 -izein 的晚期拉丁形式 -izare 提供动词词尾 -ize，也构成 organize、modernize、legalize 等词。

items.meaning: of crime; a person who offends
items.example: The base word supplies the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 词基提供主要含义。

items.meaning: to make; to cause to be
items.example: The suffix turns a noun or adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词或形容词变成动词。

items.example: The chamber criminalized the trade.
items.exampleCN: 议事厅把这种交易入罪。

items.example: The clause criminalizes late filing.
items.exampleCN: 该条款把逾期申报定为犯罪。

items.example: The practice was criminalized last year.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法去年被入罪。

items.meaning: in the act of making an offence
items.example: A criminalizing amendment was tabled.
items.exampleCN: 一项入罪化修正案被提交。

items.meaning: the act of making an offence
items.example: Criminalization changed the market.
items.exampleCN: 入罪化改变了市场。

items.example: The state decriminalized small amounts.
items.exampleCN: 该州把小额持有去罪化。

definition_zh: 违法行为；罪行；冒犯；进攻（美式拼写，英式作 offence）
definition_en: a crime or illegal act, or something that hurts or angers someone
core_image: 一张写满条款的罚单被推到当事人面前，对面的人皱起眉
scene: 社区会议上，一位居民把违规停车的照片摊在桌上，要求物业给出处理办法。Parking without a permit is a minor offense in this district.
sceneCN: 这里 offense 指依法可罚的违法行为（第 1 个义项：可受处罚的违法行为）；句意为在本区无证停车属于轻微违法。图中可辨识物件：照片、罚单、会议桌、停车标志。

pos.zh: 违法行为；罪行（美式拼写）
冒犯；进攻；令人反感的事物

senses.title: A punishable illegal act
senses.definition: an act that breaks the law and can be punished
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律并可受处罚的行为
senses.example: Parking without a permit is a minor offense in this district.
senses.exampleCN: 在本区无证停车属于轻微违法。
senses.why: Latin offensa meant 'a striking against': an offence is conduct that strikes against a rule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 offensa 意为「撞上、触犯」：违法行为就是撞上规则的行为。

senses.title: An act of insult
senses.definition: something said or done that hurts or angers another person
senses.definitionCN: 伤害或激怒他人的言行
senses.example: He took her remark as an offense and left the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把她那句话当作冒犯，离开了餐桌。
senses.why: The same image of striking against serves here: the blow lands on a person rather than on a rule.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「撞上」的形象在此落在人身上，而不是落在规则上。

senses.title: The attacking side in sport
senses.definition: the team or players whose job is to score
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中负责得分的一方或球员
senses.example: Their offense scored on the first possession.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的进攻组在第一次进攻中就得分了。
senses.why: Military attack language moved into sport, where the offense is the side that strikes.
senses.whyCN: 军事攻击的说法进入体育，那里「进攻」指负责击打的一方。

senses.title: A military attack
senses.definition: a planned attack by armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装力量有计划的攻击
senses.example: The offense began at dawn along the eastern ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 攻势在黎明沿东侧山脊开始。
senses.why: The military sense keeps the original image of a blow, aimed across a line at an enemy.
senses.whyCN: 军事义保留了「一击」的原初形象，越过界线打向敌方。

senses.title: Something repellent
senses.definition: a thing that disgusts or offends the senses
senses.definitionCN: 令感官或情感反感的事物
senses.example: The smell was an offense to everyone in the carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味让车厢里所有人都难受。
senses.why: The noun can name the source of the displeasure, not only the act that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指引起不快的行为，也能指不快本身的来源。

senses.title: A moral or religious transgression
senses.definition: a wrong considered against a moral or religious standard
senses.definitionCN: 依道德或宗教标准认定的过错
senses.example: In the old rite, the offense required a public apology.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧礼仪中，这种过失需要公开道歉。
senses.why: A moral code can be struck against just as a statute can, so the religious sense needs no courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 道德准则也会被「撞上」，正如法条会被撞上，因此宗教义不需要法庭。

senses.title: The state of being offended
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase take offense: to feel insulted
senses.definitionCN: 在「感到受辱」这一固定说法中，指被冒犯的状态
senses.example: She took offense at the question and did not answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个问题感到被冒犯，没有回答。
senses.why: The noun names not only the blow but the state of the one who received it, hence the fixed phrase for feeling insulted.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词不只指那一击，也指受击者的状态，因此有了表示「感到受辱」的固定说法。

senses.title: An attacking formation
senses.definition: the organised pattern or plan a team uses to attack
senses.definitionCN: 球队用于进攻的组织方式或计划
senses.example: The coach rebuilt the offense around two fast wings.
senses.exampleCN: 教练围绕两名快翼重建了进攻体系。
senses.why: Strategy talk turns the attacking side into a system with a name.
senses.whyCN: 战术话语把进攻方变成一个有名目的体系。

intro.en: Offense comes through Old French offense from Latin offensa 'a striking against, an injury, displeasure', from offendere, built on ob- 'against' and fendere 'to strike'. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: offense 经古法语 offense 来自拉丁 offensa「撞击、伤害、不快」，出自 offendere，由 ob-「对着」与 fendere「击打」构成，十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fendere meant 'to strike'; it also underlies defend, where de- adds the sense of striking away.
items.cn: fendere 意为「击打」；它也是 defend 的词根，那里 de- 增添「打回去」的意思。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus fendere gave offendere 'to strike against, to attack, to displease'.
items.cn: ob-「对着」加 fendere 构成 offendere「撞上、攻击、使不快」。

items.en: The noun offensa named a blow, an injury and the displeasure that followed.
items.cn: 名词 offensa 指一次撞击、一处伤害，以及随之而来的不快。

items.en: Old French offense carried both the legal and the personal senses into English.
items.cn: 古法语 offense 把法律义与个人感受义一并带入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century offense named the attacking half of a team, borrowing the military image.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，offense 指球队的进攻一半，借用了军事意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of fendere is unsettled, so any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction; the exact first English citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：fendere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的更古老词根都属于重构；英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the fendere stock, where prefixes reverse the direction of the blow; group two holds words for a breach or an insult.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 fendere 词干的词，前缀改变击打的方向；第二组是表示违法或冒犯的词。

entries.definition: The verb 'to strike against': to hurt someone's feelings or to break a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 「撞上去」的动词：伤害他人感受或违反规则。

entries.definition: De- 'away' plus fendere: to strike the blow away, hence to protect.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 fendere：把击打挡开，因此指防御。

entries.definition: The party who defends in a case; the word comes from defending, not from offending.
entries.definitionCN: 案件中作辩护的一方；这个词来自「防御」而非「冒犯」。

entries.definition: The adjective of offense, used for insults, attacks and attacking play.
entries.definitionCN: offense 的形容词，用于侮辱、攻击与进攻打法。

entries.definition: Any punishable illegal act; an offense may be minor, regulatory or military.
entries.definitionCN: 任何可罚的违法行为；offense 可以是轻微、规章性或军事性的。

entries.definition: A breaking of a specific rule or right, often administrative.
entries.definitionCN: 违反某条具体规则或权利，常属行政性质。

entries.definition: A remark that belittles a person, with no legal or military sense.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低他人的话语，不含法律或军事含义。

entries.definition: Bad conduct judged morally, which may or may not be an offense in law.
entries.definitionCN: 从道德上评判的不良行为，未必构成法律上的违法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ob- 'against' plus fendere 'strike': a blow aimed at a rule or a person.
normal.cn: ob-「对着」加 fendere「击打」：朝规则或朝人打去的一击。

normal.en: The family runs offend, offense, offensive, offender, offended.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 offend、offense、offensive、offender 与 offended。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: criminal offense, take offense, no offense.
normal.cn: 固定搭配切分义项：刑事罪行、感到被冒犯、无意冒犯。

normal.en: American spelling offense, British spelling offence; both are the same word.
normal.cn: 美式拼作 offense，英式拼作 offence，是同一个词。

normal.en: Defend uses the same root with the opposite prefix: the blow is struck away.
normal.cn: defend 用同一词根加相反前缀：把击打挡开。

abstract.en: Picture a hand striking a rulebook and then striking a person's pride.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手先打在规则手册上，又打在人的自尊上。

abstract.en: Picture a field split in two, one half pushing forward and one half holding.
abstract.cn: 想象球场分成两半，一半向前推，一半守住。

abstract.en: Picture a smell that enters a closed carriage and offends everyone in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一股气味进入密闭车厢，冒犯了里面所有人。

examples.en: The regulations list each offense and the fine attached to it.
examples.cn: 规章列出了每一项违法行为及对应的罚款。

examples.en: He apologised at once, saying he had meant no offense.
examples.cn: 他立刻道歉，说自己并无冒犯之意。

examples.en: The team's offense controlled the ball for most of the second half.
examples.cn: 该队的进攻组在下半场大部分时间控制着球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「of（对着）+ fense（打）」——对着规则或人打过去：违法、冒犯、进攻

root: 拉丁 offensa「撞击、伤害、不快」= ob-（对着）+ fendere（击打）的过去分词 offensus；fendere 更深来源不确定。英语经古法语 offense 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one blow: it lands on a rule and becomes an offence, on a person and becomes an insult, then on a scoreboard, a battlefield, the senses, a moral code, one's own pride and finally a plan for attacking.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一击：打在规则上成为违法，打在个人身上成为冒犯，再打向记分牌、战场、感官、道德准则、自己的自尊，最后成为一种进攻方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ticket pushed across a table, with the other person's brow already lowering.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张罚单被推到桌子对面，对面的人已经皱起了眉。

branches.en: THE BLOW ON A RULE: conduct strikes a statute and becomes punishable.
branches.cn: 打在规则上：行为撞上法条，因而可受处罚。

branches.en: THE BLOW ON A PERSON: the same strike lands on feelings and becomes insult.
branches.cn: 打在个人身上：同一击落在情感上，成为冒犯。

branches.en: THE ORGANISED BLOW: a team and an army both keep a side whose job is to strike.
branches.cn: 有组织的一击：球队与军队都保留负责击打的一方。

branches.en: THE SOURCE AND THE SIN: a smell can repel the senses, and a moral code can name a transgression.
branches.cn: 来源与罪过：气味能令感官反感，道德准则也能指认过失。

branches.en: ONE'S OWN STATE AND THE PLAN: a person takes offence, and a coach designs an offence.
branches.cn: 自身状态与方案：个人会感到被冒犯，教练则设计进攻方案。

intro.en: Offense is a Latin noun whose prefix and root reverse direction to build defend as well.
intro.cn: offense 是一个拉丁名词，其前缀与词根换个方向也构成 defend。

latinIntro.en: Latin fendere 'to strike' gives offend, offense and defensive words; ob- aims the blow forward, de- strikes it away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fendere「击打」衍生 offend、offense 与一批防御类词；ob- 把击打朝前送去，de- 则把它格开。

items.structure: ob- (Latin prefix, assimilated to of- before f)
items.example: The prefix aims the blow at something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把击打对准某物。

items.example: The root carries the physical blow.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着实在的一击。

items.example: The joke offended two listeners.
items.exampleCN: 这个玩笑冒犯了两名听众。

items.meaning: a blow, an injury, a breach
items.example: The offense carried a small fine.
items.exampleCN: 这项违法行为附带小额罚款。

items.example: The list named four offenses.
items.exampleCN: 清单列了四项违法行为。

items.example: The remark was openly offensive.
items.exampleCN: 那句话公然带有冒犯性。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the law
items.example: The offender paid the fine.
items.exampleCN: 违法者缴了罚款。

items.example: Counsel defended the shopkeeper.
items.exampleCN: 律师为店主辩护。
